ipd_frac_multi_peak 1.0, bp_rp_excess 2.09, |b| < 5 deg
Paired FoV1/FoV2 transits agree closely

explanation: A dusty, heavily reddened long-period variable (Mira-type AGB star) in the Galactic plane. BP-RP 5.65, G-Ks about 7.4 and a mid-IR excess out to W4 fit a cool giant with a circumstellar dust shell. G swings by a factor of about 12 (about 2.7 mag), with repeated maxima (t=0, 544, 875) and minima (168, 409, 733, 966), consistent with a period of roughly 300 d and the cycle-to-cycle changes in amplitude that Miras show. RP swings less than G and BP swings far more, as expected for a cool pulsator, and W2 varies by about a factor of 3. The flagged 'drop' (depth 0.08 +/- 0.18) is just one stretch of this pulsation, sampled sparsely, and is not significant on its own.

discriminating_test: Check ZTF g/r photometry from 2018 on for a rotation period and wandering mean level that is redder when fainter (spots), or obtain one spectrum for chromospheric activity (H-alpha / Ca II emission); a grey, non-modulated long fade would instead point to an occultation.

evidence.feature: Visit-to-visit scatter 1.26% vs epoch errors ~0.25%; 3-4% swings on ~50 d timescales before the fade
Late low state (t=807-877) at ~0.95 in both fov 1 and fov 2 and in BP and RP
BP/RP depth ratio 1.14+-0.35 (z_grey 0.39, z_dust -1.62)
W1 at t=761 (1.022+-0.019) not dimmed while BP/RP at t=752 are ~0.96
NEOWISE W1 slope -0.011+-0.013/yr lies between grey (-0.024) and temperature (-0.007) predictions
Photospheric Ks-W1 ~0.2 and W1-W2 ~-0.1; no IR excess
Absolute G ~3.4-4.3 at 2.5 kpc with moderate reddening: dwarf or subgiant, not a red giant
Single bright transit at t=0 with BP/RP excess larger than G, and RP outliers at t=114; low galactic latitude
ruwe 1.02, ipd_frac_multi_peak 0
Flat ~5% low state lasting >70 d would need <1 km/s crossing for a stellar-size occulter

explanation: Most likely intrinsic variability of an active, spotted star (M_G about 4.3 before extinction at 2.5 kpc with bp_rp 1.41, so a reddened K subgiant or dwarf, plausibly RS CVn-like). The star already varies by 3-4% over weeks (sigma_visit 1.26% against errors of about 0.25%; 1.03 to 0.99 to 1.04 between t=323 and 430). The 5-6% fall in mean level over 2.4 yr reads as spot or activity-cycle evolution. Both fields of view agree at the 0.95 level, and G, BP and RP all dim, so a calibration offset is unlikely. The BP/RP ratio of 1.14+-0.35 fits spots or grey. W1 is not dimmed at t=761, although BP/RP were already about 5% down at t=752, which weakly argues against grey occultation. There is no IR excess.

discriminating_test: Get the per-transit Gaia scan angles and check Gaia DR3/Pan-STARRS for a neighbour within ~3 arcsec. If G flux correlates with scan angle and ZTF PSF photometry (~2 arcsec) is flat, it is blending. If ZTF shows the same fast 10-25% variability and a long-term level change, it is intrinsic.

evidence.feature: phot_bp_rp_excess_factor 2.28 for bp_rp 0.78, far above the ~1.2 of an isolated star
Flux changes of 10-27% between paired transits 106.5 min apart, both up (681.26: 1.259) and down (693.26: 0.869, 605.75: 0.893)
n_above_3sigma 5 vs n_below_3sigma 1: excursions are mostly brightenings, as added neighbour flux gives
Detected 'drop' set by only 6 early visits (days 0-208) averaging ~1.08 with scatter 0.95-1.25, then a flat level for 570 days; abbe 0.67, not a smooth fade
Single step-like change with no recurrence, depth 0.12, lasting at least 572 d to the end of the data
Parallax SNR 5.1 and ruwe 1.14
|b| 5-10 deg at 2600 pc puts the star a few hundred pc from the plane, away from most star-forming regions
Large scatter on hour timescales (robust_sigma 0.041 vs errors 0.009) could also be intrinsic fast variability
No BP/RP depths, no 2MASS/WISE match, no NEOWISE or ZTF epochs: colour and energy-budget tests are unavailable

explanation: Most likely a Gaia blending/crowding artefact. The BP/RP excess factor of 2.28 at bp_rp 0.78 (about 1.2 expected for an isolated star) means a neighbour or extended flux within about 2-3 arcsec. G epochs jump 10-27% between transits only 106.5 min apart, in both directions (1.259 beside 0.990; 0.869 between 0.979 and 0.963), as contaminating flux entering or leaving the window does. The 'drop' is not a dip: the first six visits (days 0-208) sit about 8-10% high with large scatter, then the star is flat near 1.0 for 570 days. With no BP/RP depths, IR, NEOWISE or ZTF data, intrinsic variability (YSO, CV-like eruptive, pulsator) cannot be excluded.

discriminating_test: Run a period search on the ~600 ZTF r and g epochs (or check the Gaia RR Lyrae classification for this source). A 0.25-0.65 d period with an RRc/RRab light-curve shape and g amplitude greater than r would confirm pulsation. An EW-like double-humped curve with equal colours would instead favour a contact binary.

evidence.feature: Flux changes of 20-30% between transits 106.5 min to 6 h apart, in every band
Amplitude BP > G > RP at every transit (BP swing ~0.35, RP ~0.21): brighter means bluer
Distance 5100 pc and G 14.3 give M_G ~0.6 with bp_rp 0.85; |b| 20-25 deg puts it in the halo
ZTF g robust sigma 0.20 vs r 0.12, fluxes piled up near 0.80 and 1.15
Slow-change fade is only 4 visits, phase-random means of a 0.3 flux-amplitude variable; slope_z 0.42
NEOWISE W1/W2 unchanged during the fade; no IR excess from Ks to W2
Single BP 2.36 outlier at t=570.29 with no RP counterpart
ruwe 0.99, ipd_frac_multi_peak 0, bp_rp excess 1.21

explanation: The star is a large-amplitude short-period pulsator, most likely an RR Lyrae (RRc-like). At 5.1 kpc, G=14.3 gives M_G of about 0.6, the horizontal-branch value, and the star sits about 2 kpc out of the plane. Flux swings by about 30% within hours, for example 1.17 to 0.89 between transits on day 295. BP swings more than G, and G more than RP (BP/RP amplitude about 1.6, brighter when hotter), which is a temperature change, not occultation. ZTF g scatters more than r and clusters at both extremes, as a sinusoidal pulsator does. The flagged 178 d 'repeat' fade is visit means landing at random pulsation phases. The colour test is uninformative, NEOWISE shows no change and ZTF after 2020 shows no trend.

discriminating_test: Look in TESS or dense ZTF data for a rotation period of a few days, and take a low-resolution spectrum for Ca II H&K or H-alpha emission. An active, rotating star would confirm that spot-driven fades lasting months explain the Gaia dip. Also check the per-transit scan angles of the Gaia epochs between t=380 and t=587 for a blend.

evidence.feature: ZTF g and r show fades and brightenings of about 1-3% lasting months, same sign in both bands and with g amplitude about 1.5-2 times r, at times outside the Gaia dip
Gaia dip spans 5 consecutive visits with a smooth decline (abbe 0.405, about 5 sigma against the out-of-dip scatter), seen in both fields of view and in BP (depth 1.1 +/- 0.6%)
Same-epoch fov1/fov2 pairs differ by up to 1.3% (6x the quoted errors), with no consistent sign by field of view, so per-transit noise is underestimated
ipd_frac_multi_peak 0, ruwe 0.94, normal BP/RP excess factor 1.2
Duration of 207 days or more at about 1% depth: t ~ 2R/v needs v ~ 0.1 km/s for an occulter the size of the star
Photospheric Ks-W1 and W1-W2; NEOWISE W1/W2 unchanged during the dip; a 1000 K shell is excluded (W2 predicted +29%, observed -2 +/- 4%)
BP/RP depth ratio 20 +/- 167 and RP depth 0.06 +/- 0.46%: colour gives no constraint
Calibration drift shared by stars of similar magnitude and colour already removed from G, BP and RP

explanation: A roughly solar-type, slightly evolved star with no infrared excess shows one smooth Gaia fade of about 1% (visit means go from ~1.003 down to ~0.989 between t=380 and t=587 and are back by t=733). It appears in both fields of view and in BP, so it is not a single-transit defect. ZTF never overlaps the Gaia dip, but in later years it shows fades and brightenings of about 1-3% lasting months, with the same sign in g and r and deeper in g (e.g. t~2945-2990 low, t~3650-3860 high). So the dip most likely comes from the star's own slow variability, probably changing spot or facula coverage. A calibration drift or a scan-angle blend that varies with time cannot be ruled out without scan angles. An occultation lasting more than 200 days would need a very large, slow occulter.

discriminating_test: Extend the light curve past Gaia's span with ZTF r/i or near-infrared survey photometry, checking whether the fade reverses quasi-periodically on 100-1000 d timescales with the same G/RP-like chromatic amplitude ratio, as a semi-regular or long-secondary-period AGB variable would.

evidence.feature: BP-RP 6.02, G-Ks 7.8, |b| < 5 deg, parallax_snr 1.1: distant, reddened luminous red giant
W1-W2 = -0.06 (photospheric), small W3/W4 excess typical of a dusty AGB envelope rather than a young disk
G and RP rise and fall together between visits (t=0 to 34 drop, t=219 peak, t=957 low); robust sigma 0.047 (G) and 0.03 (RP) far above errors of about 0.005
G depth 0.219 vs RP depth 0.076: chromatic change, larger at shorter wavelengths
NEOWISE W1/W2 slopes consistent with zero; grey prediction (-0.083/yr) rejected at more than 5 sigma, star-temperature prediction consistent
Total amplitude about 0.3 mag over 2.6 yr, not a multi-magnitude fade
G fov-pair disagreements up to 10% (t=575, 878.8) not echoed in RP; phot_bp_rp_excess_factor 2.02 somewhat above expectation for this colour
BP essentially noise (depth 2.73 +/- 1.45, one epoch at 18.9x median at t=0.07, coincident with a high-error G point)

explanation: A heavily reddened, luminous red giant (likely AGB) in the Galactic plane: BP-RP 6.0, G-Ks 7.8, parallax unmeasurable, W1-W2 near zero (photospheric CO) with mild W3/W4 dust excess. G and RP vary together well above their errors on month timescales (e.g. bright at t=0 and t=219, faint at t=34), with abbe 0.5, as a semi-regular pulsator does. The 'trend' is the declining envelope of that variability across 18 sparse visits, perhaps part of a long secondary period. The change is chromatic (G depth about 3x RP, BP unusable), which fits TiO-driven LPV amplitudes. NEOWISE is flat, which rules out grey blocking by more than 5 sigma and fits a temperature change. The amplitude, 0.2-0.3 mag, is far too small for R CrB.

discriminating_test: Phase-fold the full ZTF g/r light curve (or one TESS sector) at P~3.4036 d. This should show a single fixed-phase, ~6-h, ~20% eclipse and a possible secondary near phase 0.5, and confirm the period against the 17-d alias.

evidence.feature: Gaia dips at 79.06, 89.49, 184.66-184.73, 225.64 fit one ephemeris P~3.404 d with ~0.26 d eclipses (ingress at 79.0-79.06, egress at 89.49-89.56 and 225.64-225.71)
Flux jumps of 8-14% within 106.5-min FOV pairs, in both FOV orderings, with normal epochs inside the 'episode' (130.4, 152.8)
Simultaneous ~15-22% dips in ZTF g, r and i (e.g. 2247.35-2247.41) and in Gaia G, BP, RP; BP/RP depth ratio 2.04+/-0.77 consistent with grey
No near- or mid-IR excess (Ks-W1=0.1, W1-W2=-0.1)
ruwe 0.978, ipd_frac_multi_peak 0, BP/RP excess factor 1.29 is normal for bp_rp 1.71; ZTF and Gaia depths agree
Depth ~20% around a luminous (~4 kpc, G=16.7) star is too deep for a planet
No brightenings above 3 sigma in G; flat outside the dips

explanation: A detached eclipsing binary. The 147-d Gaia 'episode' is really four short eclipses (79.06, 89.49, 184.7, 225.64) that Gaia happened to catch; flux changes by 8-14% between paired transits 1.8 h apart, so this is not a slow fade. By hand I found one period, P ~3.4036 d (eclipse centre T0 ~79.2, duration ~6 h, depth ~20%), that fits all four Gaia events and nearly every faint ZTF g/r/i epoch from t=1372 to 4054. Consecutive ZTF detections fall 17 d (5P) apart because of nightly sampling. The dips are grey (BP/RP ratio 2.0+/-0.8, consistent with 1) and show in G, BP, RP and ZTF g, r, i together. The star has no infrared excess, ruwe ~1, and no sign of a blend.

discriminating_test: Get a spectrum (or check archival Gaia XP / survey spectra) for luminosity class and chromospheric activity (Ca II H&K and IRT emission, H-alpha, v sin i), and run a periodogram on the dense ZTF r/i data for a 20-100 d rotation signal. Together these separate a spotted active giant from irregular giant pulsation, and both from a reddened hot star.

evidence.feature: Smooth rise then 8% decline over ~420 d in G, BP and RP, both FoVs, abbe 0.06
ZTF g/r show repeated non-periodic brightenings and fades of 5-10% on 100s of days, with g amplitude about 1.5x r
BP/RP depth ratio 1.44 +/- 0.26 (z_grey 1.7, z_dust -1.0), consistent with a temperature change
Ks=8.78 at 1100 pc implies M_K about -1.9: a moderate-luminosity K giant, not an M giant; active spotted giants vary like this
No IR excess (Ks-W3 about 0.5, W1-W2 about 0.03, consistent with reddening alone)
NEOWISE W1 +0.011 +/- 0.009 in the fade (one visit); grey blocking predicted -0.045
ruwe 1.04, ipd_frac_multi_peak 0, BP/RP excess factor as expected for this colour
No strong periodicity (s_rep 3.58 at 29.7 d), no recurrence of fixed-depth dips

explanation: A heavily reddened giant (G=14.6, Ks=8.78 at 1.1 kpc in the plane, so M_K about -1.9 and A_V about 5) varying slowly on its own. The Gaia 'fade' is the falling half of a slow cycle: G rises to 1.02 near day 490, then falls smoothly to 0.94 (abbe 0.06). The fall shows in G, BP and RP and in both fields of view. BP/RP = 1.44, which fits a temperature change. ZTF independently shows swings in both directions of about 5-10% over hundreds of days (bright near days 1300 and 2200, faint near 2850). An occulter cannot brighten the star. There is no IR excess and the astrometry is clean, so this is intrinsic semi-regular or irregular giant variability, or spot evolution on an active giant.

discriminating_test: Run a period search on the ZTF g/r (or TESS) light curve, or on the Gaia G epochs, for a strict short period that puts all nine faint transits into one or two narrow eclipse phases with a stable depth profile. In the same check, see whether the faint transits share a scan angle or field of view.

evidence.feature: Faint transits at t=0, 36.6, 237, 518.6, 676.25, 684.3, 834.0, 968.1 and 991.1 are each a single transit, with normal transits 106.5 min to ~6 h on either side
At every faint transit G, BP and RP all dim by comparable fractions (e.g. 684.3: 0.68/0.65/0.71; 833.98: 0.77/0.72/0.77); separate instruments agree
RP dims as much as G, although its window is larger, which window-edge flux loss would not do
Depths vary from 8% to 32% with errors ~0.5%, not one fixed level, so a cross-match to a single neighbour does not fit
Duty cycle ~13% (9/67), and the dense 676-677 d and 684-686 d runs each hold exactly one dip: consistent with eclipses ~1 h long at a period under a few days
ruwe 1.0, ipd_frac_multi_peak 0, BP/RP excess factor 1.3 normal for bp_rp 1.9: no sign of a neighbour
M_G ~6.3-6.6 for intrinsic bp_rp ~1.8 is ~1-1.5 mag overluminous, like an unresolved near-equal binary
No IR excess (Ks-W1 ~0, W1-W2 ~-0.1), and NEOWISE shows no change
fov1 has 7 dips in 31 epochs vs fov2 2 in 36; in all 5 pairs with one faint member, the faint one is fov1
Slow-change 'repeat' at 235 d and the detected fade are built from visit means containing single-transit dips (968.1, 991.1)

explanation: A detached eclipsing binary sampled sparsely. Nine isolated transits are 8-32% faint, and each is bracketed by normal transits 106.5 min to 6 h away, so the dips are brief. In each one G, BP and RP dim together by similar, roughly grey amounts. That rules out a one-CCD hit, and window-edge loss would spare the larger BP/RP windows. The star is otherwise quiet. About 13% of epochs are faint, with depths that vary as random eclipse phases would, and the dense runs at 676 d and 684 d each catch one dip, as a period under a few days predicts. The star sits about 1-1.5 mag above the K/M main sequence, as an unresolved binary would. One thing keeps some instrumental weight: fov1 has more dips than fov2 (7/31 vs 2/36, p~0.05). The detected fade is just the dips at 968 d and 991 d.

discriminating_test: Compare FoV1 and FoV2 Gaia epoch photometry of nearby stars with similar G and colour for the same FoV1-only drift after day ~400, and check whether ZTF g/r from 2018 on show the star's level still dropping or stable.

evidence.feature: FoV1 minus FoV2 G flux about -0.37% in all six pairs after day 485, about +0.1% before
FoV2 alone drops about 0.3% between days 535 and 680; FoV1 drops about 0.75% over the span
common-mode decline of a few tenths of a percent over years on a K7 dwarf (bp_rp 1.54, M_G~7.4)
phot_bp_rp_excess_factor 1.28 (as expected for this colour), ipd_frac_multi_peak 0, ruwe 0.97
W1-W2 about -0.1, no mid-IR excess; |b| 30-35 deg, old field dwarf
BP/RP depth ratio 3.07+/-2.56: uninformative, consistent with grey, dust or cooling
NEOWISE W1 slope -0.0017+/-0.0073 per yr: too noisy to test any prediction
only 16 visits, depth 0.55% in G against sigma_visit 0.15%; smooth (abbe 0.4), no discrete dips

explanation: A 0.5% G fade over 911 d on a quiet K7 dwarf (M_G~7.4, no IR excess, ruwe 0.97, normal BP/RP excess). About half the trend is FoV-dependent: before day ~360 FoV1 and FoV2 agree (FoV1 slightly higher), but from day 485 on FoV1 sits ~0.37% below FoV2 in all six pairs. A change on the star must look the same in both FoVs, so that part is a calibration drift. What is left is a common ~0.3% step down between days 535 and 680. That is ordinary for an activity cycle or a change in spot coverage on a K/M dwarf, though it could also be leftover calibration. BP/RP colour (3.1+/-2.6) and NEOWISE slopes cannot tell the causes apart. Nothing calls for an unexplained cause.

discriminating_test: Cross-match against quasar catalogues (Milliquas, Gaia DR3 QSO candidates, SDSS/DESI spectroscopy). A spectrum with broad emission lines at a measured redshift would settle it.

evidence.feature: W1=15.8 vs G=20.5 (G-W1 ~4.7), far brighter than any photosphere with BP-RP 0.74
W1-W2=0.8, W2-W3=2.6: WISE AGN colour locus
parallax_snr 0.79, distance poorly constrained, |b| 25-30 deg
ZTF g/r/i aperiodic swings of factor ~2-3 over years, similar in all bands, recurrence not applicable
NEOWISE W1 declines alongside Gaia G during the Gaia span, smaller amplitude and lagged
Smooth G fade (abbe 0.13, slope_z -9.6) with no FoV split; both FoVs agree
phot_bp_rp_excess_factor 1.6 at G=20.5
BP/RP depth ratio 1.25 +/- 1.37, uninformative

explanation: Almost certainly a quasar/AGN, not a dimming star. At G=20.5 with BP-RP 0.74, a star should have W1 near 19, but W1=15.8 (G-W1 about 4.7). W1-W2=0.8 and W2-W3=2.6 put it right on the WISE AGN locus. Parallax is consistent with zero, and it sits at high galactic latitude. The Gaia 'trend' is smooth (abbe 0.13) and is echoed by a lagged, smaller W1 decline over the same years. ZTF then shows aperiodic, roughly achromatic changes of a factor of 2 or more over years: low in 2018-19, then brightening. That is red-noise behaviour typical of an AGN. The high BP/RP excess fits a faint source with a host galaxy or extended light. Neither eclipses nor dust fit this.

discriminating_test: Fold the full ZTF and Gaia light curve at ~490 d and check for a stable Mira-like phase curve; check a variable-star catalogue or a spectrum for M-type/TiO and Balmer emission at maximum.

evidence.feature: Smooth, large-amplitude cycle in G/BP/RP (factor ~5 in G, ~8 in BP), abbe 0.155
ZTF g repeats with a ~490 d period and amplitude up to ~60x over ~7 years
BP-RP 3.88, Ks 0.83, W3/W4 very bright: a cool, luminous, dusty AGB star
Amplitude larger in BP and ZTF g than in RP; both fields of view agree
Brightenings as large as the fades (n_above_3sigma=10, n_below=0), unlike R CrB fades from a steady maximum
ruwe 3.06 at G~9.7: could be photocentre jitter from a large, asymmetric red giant rather than an eclipsing companion

explanation: A Mira-type long-period variable caught near pulsation minimum. The star is very red (BP-RP 3.88) and luminous (Ks 0.83 at 710 pc), and very bright in the mid-infrared (W3 -1.7, W4 -2.7), which points to a dusty AGB envelope. Gaia G swings smoothly by a factor of about 5 (abbe 0.155), with maxima near t~113 and ~640 d and minima near ~390 and ~875 d. ZTF g varies by a factor of up to about 60 and repeats every ~490 d for more than five cycles (minima ~1325, ~1800, ~2300, ~2780, ~3260). The 'drop' is the falling branch into the minimum. Its amplitude is larger in BP and ZTF g than in RP, as expected for a cool pulsator, and its timing fits the cycle.

discriminating_test: Compare this star's uncorrected epoch G with the subtracted drift model, and with stars of similar magnitude and colour on the same CCDs, across t~370-640. If the steps are in the correction, the cause is processing. If they are in this star's raw G alone, the cause is a source-specific G calibration offset. An independent 2014-2017 survey such as ATLAS or ASAS-SN showing no 2% fade would confirm an artefact.

evidence.feature: G depth 0.0212+-0.0005 but RP depth 0.0005+-0.002 and BP 0.003+-0.002; no stellar change can dim G without dimming RP/BP
Change is a staircase of flat plateaus (1.014, 1.000, 0.990) with breaks only between visit groups, low in-plateau scatter
Pipeline removed calibration drift shared by similar stars from G, BP and RP; an imperfect correction affecting G alone would leave such steps
Both fields of view drop identically; FoV offset only ~0.2%
ruwe 1.05, ipd_frac_multi_peak 0, normal BP/RP excess; a neighbour would contaminate the larger BP/RP windows first, opposite to what is seen
NEOWISE W1 change +0.002+-0.009 vs grey prediction -0.021; no IR change or excess
Repeat period 603 d is just the two steps; no eclipse-like events in Gaia or ZTF
ZTF g declines ~1% after 2020 with r nearly flat; possibly slow activity or a ZTF normalisation effect, unrelated to the Gaia G-only step

explanation: Gaia G falls in flat steps: about 1.014 until t~373, about 1.000 for t~422-577, about 0.990 from t~637 on, which is about 2.4% in total. Both fields of view show the steps equally. BP and RP do not show them: the fitted depths are 0.3+-0.2% and 0.05+-0.2%, and my own plateau means give RP flat to about 0.15%. For a K dwarf most of the G flux is RP light, so a real 2.4% change in the star's light, whether grey, dusty or from cooling, would have to appear in RP at about 17 sigma. A drop seen only in G, made of flat plateaus with breaks between groups of visits, looks like a G-band calibration-epoch offset or an artefact of the drift correction. ruwe 1.05 and ipd_frac_multi_peak 0 argue against a blend. NEOWISE is flat.

discriminating_test: Check the 2023-24 unWISE/NEOWISE W2 images for a blended red neighbour or faint-source (Eddington) bias, and take one current 3-5 micron measurement (for example SPHEREx or ground-based L/M). A confirmed, growing warm excess on the star would establish circumstellar dust re-radiating the missing light (debris or disk), while no excess would favour a cold foreground or disk occulter.

evidence.feature: Gaia G linear fade (slope_z -30.9, abbe 0.034) continued at a similar rate in ZTF r and faster in ZTF g over 2018-2025
Same trend in independent instruments (Gaia G/BP/RP, ZTF g/r) with per-field ZTF normalisation
Chromatic depth: BP 0.026 vs RP 0.006 in the episode; ZTF dg/dr ~1.7 mag ratio
Colour ratio steeper than stellar cooling (~1.3); visit noise 0.0019 and no spot modulation in dense Gaia/ZTF sampling
NEOWISE W2 rising from ~0.85 (2014) to 1.43-1.58 (2023-24) while W1 stays near flat
No near/mid-IR excess in 2MASS/AllWISE (Ks-W1 ~0, W1-W2 -0.1, W3 upper limit)
ruwe 0.95, ipd_frac_multi_peak 0, FoV pairs agree, BP/RP excess 1.21 normal
Parallax SNR 23 at 1.4 kpc gives M_G ~3-4: a dwarf or subgiant, not a giant
Monotonic decade-long fade with no recurrence and no deep fast drops

explanation: The detected dip is part of a smooth, steady fade lasting a decade: Gaia G falls 1.75%/yr (abbe 0.03, slope_z -31), and ZTF continues it from 2018 to 2025 (g -18%, r -11%). Because the instruments agree, artefacts are unlikely. The star is quiet: it shows no rotational modulation, the fields of view agree, ruwe is 0.95 and there is no multi-peak. It is a reddened F/G dwarf or subgiant (M_G ~3-4). The fade is chromatic: BP fades more than G, and G more than RP; in ZTF dg/dr is about 1.7, steeper than both interstellar dust and stellar cooling (~1.3). ZTF 2018-2023 shows no change. A monotonic, FoV-independent decay across many scan configurations argues against scan-angle blending, and a G change larger than RP argues against a window blend. The shape fits a low-magnification microlensing tail (u0~2.2, tE~60 d) or a fading brightening of the star or an unresolved companion. The colour (BP/RP 2.1+-1.1) cannot tell grey from dust or temperature. There is no IR excess and the star is quiet. An early-mission Gaia calibration residual remains a serious alternative.

discriminating_test: Compare the G visit means with those of nearby field stars of the same magnitude and colour that share the same scans, then extend the baseline with Gaia DR4 or ZTF and a Ca II H&K activity time series. A drift shared by the field stars means it is instrumental. A turnover tied to an activity change means it is a stellar cycle.

evidence.feature: Slow fade of a few mmag on a K-dwarf main-sequence star, typical of an activity cycle
Trend amplitude near the mmag level of residual Gaia DR3 photometric systematics; dense scan groups sit slightly brighter than neighbouring sparse visits
Fade seen in both fov 1 and fov 2 late epochs; no persistent FOV offset
BP and RP group means jump by about 0.5% between dense groups while G does not, so the BP/RP colour of the change is unreliable
ratio_bp_over_rp 1.79 +/- 2.47; z_grey 0.32, z_dust 0.04: colour undetermined
No IR excess in Ks/W1-W3 and W4 only an upper limit; quiet field star at |b| 25-30 deg
ruwe 1.03, ipd_frac_multi_peak 0, normal BP/RP excess factor: no resolved neighbour or astrometric companion
Abbe 0.52 and the rebound at 833-835 d: red-noise wander, not a clean secular decline
Parallax SNR 95 at 470 pc

explanation: A 0.4% G fade over 2.7 yr (0.15%/yr) in a quiet K dwarf (BP-RP 1.26, M_G about 6.5, ruwe 1.03, no IR excess). The fade is not monotonic: the dense 833-835 d group is back near 1.000 between low visits at 765-788 and 882-934 d, and Abbe 0.52 shows red noise, so the formal slope_z of -4.5 overstates the significance. Both fields of view fade the same way. The BP/RP ratio (1.8 +/- 2.5) and the NEOWISE slope cannot tell grey, dust or temperature apart. The most likely cause is a magnetic activity cycle (spot or facula coverage changing). The next most likely is a residual Gaia calibration drift at the mmag level. A dust occulter is not needed.

discriminating_test: Run a strict period search (BLS or PDM) on the combined Gaia and ZTF dip epochs and fold them: a single period near 0.375 d or 0.75 d, with or without a secondary eclipse, that puts every deep epoch in narrow phase windows would confirm the eclipsing binary; no consistent period would raise unexplained or artefact classes.

evidence.feature: Dip at t=804.13 equally deep in G, BP and RP (~0.70-0.72); also grey at t=0.25 (0.49/0.46/0.50) and t=110.82
Dips last less than one 6-h spin interval and have normal epochs on both sides; depths up to ~51%
In the first 2 days, dips every 0.75 d in each field of view with depths changing smoothly (0.49->0.63->0.83 and 0.98->0.91->0.75)
Many deep one-night dips in ZTF g and r over ~1900 d, identical in exposure pairs 40 s apart, spacings close to whole days
ZTF PSF photometry at 2 arcsec shows full depth; ipd_frac_multi_peak 0; ruwe 0.97
Detected 'episode' depth of 0.081 comes from one eclipse epoch averaged with normal visits; slow-change trigger was 'repeat' at 57 d
Ks-W1 0.1 and W1-W2 0.0: no infrared excess

explanation: A short-period detached eclipsing binary. The flagged 119-day 'episode' is really one eclipse epoch (t=804.13, G 0.724, BP 0.700, RP 0.704, grey) averaged with normal visits, and the 57 d 'repeat' is an alias. The dense early Gaia sampling shows deep (up to 51%), grey, single-transit dips every 0.75 d in both fields of view. Their depths change smoothly from one dip to the next, as when a narrow eclipse is sampled at a nearly commensurate period (probably near 0.375 or 0.75 d). ZTF PSF photometry at 2 arcsec shows many one-night dips of 30-48% in g and r between normal nights. Their spacings are close to whole days, the usual aliasing for a sub-day period. There is no IR excess.

discriminating_test: Check a long-baseline ZTF r/i (or ASAS-SN / near-IR) light curve after t=967 for the predicted rise back to maximum at about the same 3-4 mag amplitude within ~100-250 d, which would confirm a ~400-550 d Mira cycle; also check for an M or C spectral type or an OH maser.

evidence.feature: G flux ranges 0.40-14.0 (about 3.9 mag) with repeated bright and faint phases on a ~400-550 d timescale across the whole span
bp_rp 6.1, G-Ks about 9.5, W1/W2 saturated, Ks-W4 about 3.5 mid-IR excess, low Galactic latitude
Earlier minimum at t~387-409 (flux ~0.82-0.85) resembles the detected fade (0.40-0.48), so the fade repeats as part of a cycle
G and RP fade depths agree (5.64 vs 5.55) and both fields of view track each other at every epoch
BP depth 0.24 +/- 2.75, a single 52x BP outlier at t=958.63 fov 2, bp_rp_excess 2.66: BP is unreliable for this very red source
NEOWISE W1/W2 change small (-0.13 +/- 0.28, -0.17 +/- 0.21) against an optical fade of more than 50%: typical of a Mira's small IR amplitude, not grey blocking
Minimum at t~958 is deeper than the earlier one, which leaves room for extra circumstellar dust obscuration

explanation: An extremely red (BP-RP 6.1, G-Ks about 9.5), mid-IR-bright star in the Galactic plane, with Ks-W4 excess from circumstellar dust: a dusty AGB/Mira-type long-period variable. Across the whole Gaia span G swings by a factor of about 35 (about 3.9 mag): maxima near t~170 and t~600, minima near t~390-410 and t~960, so the cycle is roughly 400-550 d (s_rep period 350 d). The detected 'fade' is just the latest pulsation minimum, normalised against a median inflated by bright phases. G and RP depths match. BP is noise-dominated (huge error, one 52x single-epoch outlier, excess factor 2.66). The small W1/W2 change fits Mira IR amplitudes, which are far below the optical ones. A deeper-than-usual minimum could include some dust obscuration.

discriminating_test: Plot per-epoch G flux against Gaia scan angle, and look at a deep high-resolution image (Pan-STARRS/DECaPS) for a neighbour within about 2-4 arcsec. If the bright epochs line up with the scan angles where that neighbour falls in the window, this is a blend. A flat ZTF PSF light curve would confirm it.

evidence.feature: ruwe 2.24, ipd_frac_multi_peak 6, phot_bp_rp_excess_factor 1.98 at bp_rp 1.07, |b| 0-5 deg
FOV pairs 106 min apart differ by 7-10% at t=632, 661, 943 (errors about 1%)
Early G epochs bright (up to 1.295) while the same transits have BP and RP at about 0.75-0.83
Abbe 0.83: the 'drop' is not a smooth change; isolated bright outliers (n_above_3sigma 9, n_below 0)
BP and RP robust sigma 0.14-0.15, far above their errors, and not coherent with G
BP/RP depth ratio 0.37 +/- 1.6, consistent with anything
No ZTF or NEOWISE data on either side of the change

explanation: This looks like a blended G=17.7 source in the Galactic plane, not a real fade. RUWE is 2.24, ipd_frac_multi_peak is 6 and the BP/RP excess factor is 1.98, so a neighbour is very likely. The 'drop' is only the early epochs being brighter by 7-30%, scattered one epoch at a time; it is not a smooth decline (Abbe 0.83). Paired transits 106 minutes apart disagree by 7-10% (t=632, 661, 943), which points to contamination that depends on scan angle or field of view. In the early bright G epochs, BP and RP are about 20% fainter, which no real brightening would do. BP and RP scatter is about 0.15 and does not move with G. The colour depths are unconstrained.

discriminating_test: Look at the ZTF g/r light curve (or Gaia scan angles at the outburst epochs together with a check for a bright neighbour within a few arcsec). Repeated, blue, few-day outbursts of about 4 mag would confirm a dwarf nova. Bright epochs tied to particular scan angles would point to a neighbour leaking into the window.

evidence.feature: G flux about 40x median at t=376 and in four consecutive transits (fov 1 and 2) over 8 h at t=862.9
Detected change has negative depth in all bands (net brightening inside 406-921 d), driven by the outburst
Outburst much stronger in BP (97x) than RP (17x) at t=376, i.e. a blue outburst
Fading from 4.5 to 1.2 to 0.8 over the first 54 d, and still at 1.8 20-58 d after the t=862 outburst
Flux constant over 8 h in both fields of view at ecliptic latitude 40-50 deg
phot_bp_rp_excess_factor 1.67 at G=20.6 and galactic latitude 5-10 deg (BP/RP contamination; outburst G change larger than BP or RP change at t=862)
Lowest points (0.72, 0.715 with err 0.20) within quiescent scatter; 27.7 d repeat from only 23 visits
No 2MASS or WISE counterpart, consistent with a faint compact binary

explanation: The 'dip' is really a brightening: depths are negative in G, BP and RP (-3.3, -3.7, -1.6) because the window 406-921 d contains a ~40x (about 4 mag) outburst at t=862.9. That outburst holds steady over four transits in both fields of view for 8 h. There is another single-transit outburst at t=376, and at t=0 the star is fading (4.5 to 1.2 to 0.8 over 54 d). The outbursts are bluer than the quiescent star (BP 97x vs RP 17x). A faint, blue-ish source low in the Galaxy that recurs in multi-day outbursts of about 4 mag looks most like a dwarf-nova cataclysmic variable. The quiescent lows near 0.72 are within the noise, and the 27.7 d 'repeat' is a fit to noise and outbursts. A bright neighbour leaking into the window is the main alternative.

discriminating_test: Get ZTF g and r light curves (2018 on) and NEOWISE photometry of nearby comparison stars. A slow change deeper in g than in r, with rotational modulation, would point to spots. Equal g and r depths with a W1 fade not shared by the comparison stars would support grey blocking.

evidence.feature: Slow fade of about 1.7% plus about 0.5% visit-to-visit excess scatter on an M dwarf, with a partial rebound around day 765-835
Depths in G, BP and RP agree (1.66%, 1.4%, 1.7%); ipd_frac_multi_peak 1%; ruwe 0.96
NEOWISE W1 slope -0.0098+/-0.0031 per year, close to the grey prediction (-0.0061) and 2.6 sigma from the star-temperature prediction (-0.0017)
W1 falls over the same years in an independent instrument, which a Gaia-only calibration drift would not do
BP/RP ratio 0.82+/-0.62: grey and stellar cooling both allowed, interstellar-like dust weakly disfavoured (z_dust -1.4)
No IR excess: W1-W2 = 0 and the W3 upper limit sits at the photosphere, so there is no warm dust and no disk
Single low G points at days 75 and 789 with no matching drop in BP/RP (BP is higher at day 789)

explanation: This is an early-M dwarf (BP-RP 1.72, M_G about 7.4, no IR excess). It fades about 1.7% over 990 d, and the fade is noisy and not monotonic: there is a rebound to 1.000 near day 765-835, and the Abbe value is 0.81. On top of that it varies by about 0.5% between visits. The most likely cause is a slow change in spot coverage (an activity cycle) on a spotted star. G, BP and RP fade alike, which argues against a blend. The BP/RP ratio cannot tell grey from a temperature change. The main tension is NEOWISE W1: it falls -0.0098+/-0.0031 per year. That fits grey blocking better than spots, which should dim W1 only by a fraction of the G change. So a grey, unexplained fade keeps real weight.

discriminating_test: A low-resolution optical spectrum: H-alpha emission with Li I 6708 absorption would confirm a young star (dust or accretion variability); broad redshifted emission lines would make it an AGN.

evidence.feature: Strong near- and mid-IR excess: W1-W2 0.8, W2-W3 2.4, W3 and W4 about 3.8 and 5.4 mag above photosphere
Irregular 10-30% fades and recoveries in ZTF g and r over 7 years, not just one Gaia episode
BP/RP depth ratio 1.37+-0.39 and ZTF g/r change ratio about 1.1-1.3: grey to mildly reddening
Shallow, slow changes (tens of per cent over months to years), not deep sudden multi-magnitude fades
600-day smooth fade with no recurrence at a fixed period; ruwe 1.02
Same variability in ZTF 2-arcsec PSF photometry and Gaia; ipd_frac_multi_peak 0, normal BP/RP excess factor
Parallax SNR 4.3 (Galactic source), although the WISE colours and red-noise variability resemble an AGN
Variability within single ZTF seasons (e.g. recovery 2100-2240 d), not only steps between fields or CCDs

explanation: Most likely a disk-bearing young star whose brightness wanders with circumstellar extinction. WISE shows a protoplanetary-disk-level excess (Ks-W1 0.7, W1-W2 0.8, W2-W3 2.4, W3-W4 1.6), far too strong for a debris disk. The Gaia 10% decline is one piece of long-term irregular variability: ZTF g and r show 10-30% fades and recoveries on month-to-year timescales over 2700 d, seen in both bands. The colour ratio (BP/RP 1.37+-0.39, ZTF g/r about 1.1-1.3) points to grey-to-moderately reddening dust, which is typical of disk grains. Clean astrometry (ruwe 1.02, no multi-peak) and agreement between Gaia and ZTF rule out blends or calibration steps. An AGN is the main alternative but is disfavoured by the 4.3-sigma parallax.

discriminating_test: Pull the per-CCD (AF1-AF9) G fluxes, scan angles and across-scan window positions for the five low transits. Then check a deep near-IR or optical image (e.g. VVV/UKIDSS/Pan-STARRS) for a neighbour within a few arcsec. Lows clustered in scan angle toward a neighbour mean crowding. Flux loss confined to window-edge or truncated-window transits means a detector or window artefact.

evidence.feature: G lows of 8-11% at t=0, 184.8, 733.5, 882.1, 911.6; RP at the same epochs -3.1% to +2.7% (mean about -1%), for a star with BP-RP=4.6 where G and RP sample mostly the same light
Same failure of colour: a G-only dip with no RP counterpart cannot be grey or dust-like occultation (dust with BP/RP~1.7 would still dim RP by several per cent)
Normal visits at 774.7, 786.7, 830.2, 845.1 inside the detected 733-912 d episode: the deficit comes from isolated single-transit outliers

Lows near multiples of ~182 d (0, 185, 733, 912); the 177 d repeat is not strict (357 d normal at phase ~0.02; 882 d off-pattern), suggesting a dependence on scan angle or scanning law rather than a true period
|b| 0-5 deg, G=18.2, phot_bp_rp_excess_factor 1.81 above the ~1.68 expected for this colour, BP outlier 9.1 at 609.27 and large-error high G points at 410.9 and 609.35
4 of the 5 low transits are in fov1, but most fov1 transits are normal
Star otherwise quiet: G robust_sigma 0.016 vs median err 0.013, RP robust_sigma 0.019 vs err 0.015, abbe 0.93, slope_z -0.2
ruwe 1.08 and ipd_frac_multi_peak 0: no clearly resolved neighbour

explanation: Most likely these are artefacts in single Gaia G transits, in a crowded field in the Galactic plane. The 178 d 'episode' is not one continuous dimming. Normal visits (774-845 d, flux 0.99-1.03) sit between isolated low transits at 0, 185, 733, 882 and 912 d. Each is 8-11% low in G while RP at the same moment stays within about 3%. For a star with BP-RP 4.6, most G light falls in RP, so the star itself cannot have dimmed. At 911.6 d the fov1 transit is 9% low and the fov2 transit 106 min later is normal. The lows fall near multiples of half a year, which fits scan geometry, and mostly in fov1. A faint star at |b|<5 deg with a raised BP/RP excess points to a neighbour cutting into the window. Otherwise the star is quiet, probably a distant reddened giant.

discriminating_test: Check a dense multi-year near-IR or mid-IR light curve (NEOWISE W1/W2 visits, or a Galactic-plane Ks survey) or the Gaia long-period-variable catalogue for a ~420-460 d periodic cycle with ~1-2 mag IR amplitude whose maxima repeat on schedule after t~1000 d. A clean recurrence would confirm a Mira.

evidence.feature: G flux ranges 0.27-10.6 (factor ~40) with smooth quasi-periodic maxima ~420 d apart and minima ~470 d apart
Very red colours (BP-RP 4.79, G-Ks ~9.7) and strong IR excess Ks-W1 ~2, W2-W3 ~1.9, W4 = 2.37
Detected dip is the declining branch to minimum at t~883, followed by recovery toward median by t~967
Paired FoV G fluxes agree closely (e.g. 875.4-875.8, 883.4, 578.0, 596.3-596.5)
RP and G rise and fall together, with amplitude larger in G than RP, as expected for a cool pulsator with TiO-sensitive blue flux
Recurring bright maxima rather than a star sitting at maximum with sudden fades
Single-FoV RP outliers (9.9 at t=0.0004, 24.6 at t=960.89), noisy BP, ipd_frac_multi_peak=1.0, BP/RP excess factor 2.93, ruwe 3.22
Colour test ratio -0.08 +/- 0.41, unphysical and driven by the corrupted BP/RP epochs
Low Galactic latitude (0-5 deg), very red and dusty, which leaves some room for an embedded young star

explanation: Most likely a dust-enshrouded Mira-type AGB star in the Galactic plane. It is extremely red (BP-RP 4.79, G-Ks ~9.7) with a strong warm-dust excess (Ks-W1 ~2, rising through W3/W4). G varies smoothly by a factor of ~40 (~4 mag). Maxima fall near t~170-200 and ~580-600, minima near ~410 and ~883, so the period is roughly 420-460 d. RP tracks G and the paired fields of view agree, which rules out a scan-angle blend. The detected 'drop' (733-968 d, minimum at 883) is just the descending branch and minimum of one pulsation cycle, and the flux is recovering by t=967. The single-FoV RP spikes (9.9 at t=0, 24.6 at t=960.9) and the noisy BP are artefacts of crowding/blending (ipd_frac_multi_peak=1, BP/RP excess 2.93), and they corrupt the colour test.

discriminating_test: Get a TESS or K2 light curve (or a Ca II H&K/X-ray activity index). Rotational spot modulation of at least about 0.5%, or high activity, would make a 1% activity-driven fade expected. Also check whether Gaia stars of similar magnitude and colour near this one share the trend.

evidence.feature: Smooth ~1% fade over ~400 d seen in both fov 1 and fov 2, low abbe 0.385
BP depth 1.19%, RP 0.70%, G 0.89% (ratio 1.71 +/- 0.67): redder when fainter, grey only 1 sigma off
NEOWISE W1 change +0.002 +/- 0.007 vs grey prediction -0.009; 1000 K shell prediction (W1 +0.095, W2 +0.21) excluded
Flat Ks-W1-W2-W3 colours, no infrared excess, main-sequence absolute magnitude
404 d duration of a monotonic fade, ruwe 1.05
ipd_frac_multi_peak 0, normal bp_rp_excess_factor 1.23
Single transit at t=516.6 with BP -3%, RP -1.2%, G -0.9%, followed by normal flux at t=545
Only 17 Gaia visits; trend is ~0.5%/yr and fade is open-ended (faint to last visit); calibration drift removal is model-dependent
ZTF 2018+ quiet at its ~1.4% noise level, per-field normalisation prevents tying its level to Gaia's

explanation: An ordinary early-K dwarf (M_G about 5.5, bp_rp 1.13, ruwe 1.05, no IR excess) shows a slow, smooth fade of about 1% (abbe 0.385, slope_z -4.9), mostly after day 680. Both fields of view show it, so it is not an FoV offset. It gets redder as it fades (BP/RP ratio 1.71 +/- 0.67), as a growing spot coverage or activity-cycle change would. NEOWISE W1 shows no grey-like dimming and no hot dust; this fits the star cooling or a thin screen of dust in front. A 404 d timescale rules out eclipses. At this level the star's own magnetic variability is the simplest cause. A leftover Gaia calibration drift, or dust, cannot be ruled out. The single chromatic transit at day 516 may be an artefact.

discriminating_test: Take one new JHKs epoch and compare it with 2MASS Ks=15.0 (1998-2001), together with archival Pan-STARRS1 multi-epoch grizy. These show when the fade began and whether it stays grey into the near-IR. Add a low-resolution spectrum to confirm a main-sequence dwarf and to check for youth or activity indicators.

evidence.feature: Same ~2%/yr decline in Gaia G, ZTF g/r and NEOWISE W1/W2 over ~11 yr
Decline is grey: ZTF g/r slope ratio ~1.03, change ratio 1.09; W1 fades as much as G (dust-in-front predicts W1 ~7% of G)
W1 dims about as much as optical, not ~1/3 as a cooling photosphere would
No IR excess: Ks-W1 0.1, W1-W2 0.1, W3/W4 only upper limits; no W1/W2 brightening that a re-emitting 300-1000 K shell would cause
ruwe 1.02, ipd_frac_multi_peak 0, equal fractional fade in 0.1 arcsec Gaia and 6 arcsec WISE apertures
M_G ~5 dwarf at 1600 pc (not a giant or a B star); smooth, no periodicity (s_rep null)
Linear, curvature-free fade over >11 yr would need an implausibly slow sharp edge; it needs a smooth optical-depth gradient

explanation: A smooth, roughly linear fade of about 2%/yr, starting before Gaia and still going in 2025: Gaia G (slope_z -20, abbe 0.06), ZTF g and r (-0.0216 and -0.021/yr) and NEOWISE W1 (about 20% over 9 yr). The fade is grey from g to W1 (g/r about 1.05, W1 dims about as much as G), so small-grain dust in front and a cooling star are both ruled out, and three independent instruments make an instrumental cause unlikely. The star looks like an ordinary G/K dwarf (M_G about 5) with no IR excess. The best listed fit is a slow ingress into a grey, large-grain or clumpy occulter with an extended column-density gradient (disk_occultation), but no curvature and no recovery are seen, so a large unexplained share remains.

discriminating_test: Check ZTF g/r photometry from 2018 on (and NEOWISE W1/W2) for whether the fade continues, recovers like the egress of an occultation, or reverses colour. Also check Gaia neighbours of similar magnitude and colour for a matching residual trend.

evidence.feature: BP/RP depth ratio 0.85+-0.27 (z_grey -0.55, z_dust -3.14)
Ratio 2.2 sigma below the ~1.45 expected for cooling/spots
Smooth decelerating fade, abbe 0.08, slope_z -9.1, no recurrence
FoV 1 and 2 agree within the clump at day 80-83; ipd_frac_multi_peak 0; ruwe 1.0; normal BP/RP excess
Equal depth in G, BP and RP; calibration drift already removed by the pipeline
Distance 2600 pc and G 17.1 imply a dwarf or subgiant, not a red giant
Parallax SNR 5.6
No WISE photometry and no NEOWISE visits in the change

explanation: A smooth, decelerating, monotonic fade of about 6% over 990 d (fast drop from ~1.04 to ~1.005 in the first 180 d, then ~1%/yr), with abbe 0.08 and the star otherwise quiet at the 0.4% level. G, BP and RP fall by the same amount (ratio 0.85+-0.27: grey, and dust is excluded at 3 sigma). FoV 1 and 2 agree, ipd_frac_multi_peak is 0 and ruwe is 1.0, so a blend or scan-angle artefact is unlikely. At 2600 pc the star is an F/G dwarf or subgiant, not a giant. The most likely cause is slow secular variability of the star or system, such as a grey occultation by a large-grained disk or a long-term trend. A spot cycle that large is unlikely, and there is no IR data to test a dust shell.

discriminating_test: Get a TESS or ZTF light curve and look for ~1% rotational modulation at a period of days to weeks, and check for chromospheric activity (Ca II H&K or X-ray). A clear spot period on an active K dwarf would confirm activity. A quiet, non-rotating star would raise the odds of an occultation or an artefact.

evidence.feature: Day-to-week structure inside the episode (t=293 back to ~1.001, t=300-301 at ~0.990) and visit-to-visit sigma 0.0044 vs epoch errors 0.002
Post-episode level ~1.004 above pre-episode ~1.000; positive slope 0.6%/yr (slope_z 5.6), i.e. slow activity-like drift rather than a box-shaped dip
Dip present in both fov 1 and fov 2 at t=88, 133, 141, 300
BP/RP depth ratio 2.64 +/- 1.81 (z_grey 0.9, z_dust 0.5): chromatic-leaning but not decisive
Only 2 pre-episode visits define 'normal before'; baseline poorly constrained
NEOWISE W1 'brightening' +3.7% driven by one visit with error 0.076; the precise visit (0.998 +/- 0.008) shows no change, excluding a 1000 K shell (+10% predicted)
Ks-W1 = 0.5 mag with wise_match_p 0.55 suggests WISE blending rather than real warm dust; ruwe 1.03, ipd_frac_multi_peak 0, normal BP/RP excess argue against a Gaia-level blend
Year-long duration and 1.2% depth around a K dwarf would need a large slowly crossing structure if occultation

explanation: The most likely cause is magnetic activity on a K dwarf (M_G ~6.6, BP-RP 1.36): a season of heavier spot coverage. The 1.2% low state is shallow and lasts about a year, and it has internal structure: it recovers fully at t=293 and is low again by t=300. After it the star sits slightly brighter than before, and it varies by about 0.4% from visit to visit (more than the 0.2% errors). That fits evolving spots and an activity trend, not a smooth occultation. Both fields of view show the dip, which argues against an FOV offset. BP dims more than RP (ratio 2.6±1.8), which suits cool spots but is too noisy to tell spots from dust. The precise NEOWISE visit (0.998±0.008) rules out a hot dust shell. A disk occultation is still possible.

discriminating_test: Run a strict period search on the ZTF r and g dip epochs (try ~7.0 d and its submultiples, from the 1596.65/1603.67/1610.60 spacing) and fold Gaia's dips at 222.6 and 375.3 at the best period. A coherent ephemeris with repeatable eclipse depth and shape confirms an EB; dips that do not phase up would point to a dipper or an artefact.

evidence.feature: Gaia dips at 222.6 and 375.3 are grey and simultaneous in G, BP and RP (BP/RP depth ratio near 1)
Normal Gaia visit at 244.3 between the two dips: two short events, not one 153-d episode
ZTF r high-cadence runs show smooth ingress/egress (0.29 to 0.45 in ~48 min at 1610.6; 0.51 to 0.39 at 1596.6)
Deep ZTF dips (to 0.26-0.38 in r, 0.29 in g) on isolated nights, normal on adjacent nights; same-night g and r dip at 3065.6-3065.7
Dip depth up to ~74% needs a stellar-size occulter, not a planet
Galactic plane, elevated BP/RP excess factor 1.4, no 2MASS/WISE match: crowded field
Red (bp_rp 1.94) low-latitude source with irregular deep dips; no IR data to test for a disk
Gaia otherwise fairly quiet (robust sigma 0.022, abbe 1.29, slope_z 0.33)

explanation: The 'episode' is really two separate single-transit dips (t=222.6, 30%; t=375.3, 23%), with a normal visit at 244.3 between them. Both show up in G, BP and RP at about the same depth (222.6: 0.70/0.71/0.73), so they are grey and not one-band defects. ZTF shows the same behaviour on its own: many short, deep dips confined to single nights (r down to 0.26-0.38, g down to 0.29), with smooth ingress and egress over about an hour in the high-cadence runs (1559.73, 1596.65, 1610.60), normal flux on the nights either side, and dips roughly 7 d apart at 1596.65/1603.67/1610.60. Dips lasting hours, deep, grey, with a duty cycle of about 8%, are best explained by a detached eclipsing binary that Gaia caught in partial eclipse.

discriminating_test: Check archival ASAS-SN/ATLAS/Pan-STARRS photometry from the Gaia gap (days ~338-468) for an optical outburst and for short irregular dips during the fade: an outburst points to a merger/planet engulfment (other_astrophysical), irregular dips on top of the fade to an orbiting collision cloud (debris_transit); a current mid-IR spectrum showing a silicate feature would confirm fresh small-grain dust.

evidence.feature: NEOWISE W1 0.838->1.0 (+19%) and W2 0.52->1.0 (+92%) between days 328 and 692, intermediate at 494, then flat to day 3409; neowise_change test missed it because its outside baseline is dominated by post-event visits
Added IR colour W1-W2 ~1.7 mag (~600 K blackbody; ~800 K at day 494) with luminosity ~0.04 L*, matching the 4.5% G depth (pred 600 K: W1 +21%, W2 +99% for f=0.0446)
IR rise tracks optical fade in time (W2 38% of final rise at day 494 vs G 37-40% of final depth at days 468-517)
BP/RP depth ratio 2.01+/-0.52 (z_grey 1.93, z_dust 0.60): reddened, small-grain dust-like dimming
fov 1 and fov 2 agree at every paired transit in the fade (468, 486, 517, 713, 842 d); ruwe 1.0, ipd_frac_multi_peak 0
Fade lasts >230 d to the last visit with a plateau, ZTF roughly flat 2018-2025 (ztf_after change +0.4%), W1/W2 stay elevated: persistent new state, not a recurring eclipse
M_G ~5.2 at BP-RP 1.12, 870 pc, |b| 30-35 deg (z ~460 pc): dwarf far from star-forming regions, not a supergiant
AllWISE 2010 W1-W2 = 0.0, Ks-W1 = 0.1: photospheric before the event (W3 12.3 marginal)
Absorbed fraction ~ sightline depth implies near-isotropic dust covering around a dwarf, unusual for a flat collisional ring

Decisive: NEOWISE W1 rises 19% and W2 92% over the same interval (part-way at day 494, when the fade was ~40% done) and stays high for ~8 yr. The added flux has W1-W2~1.7, a ~600 K emitter whose luminosity (~4% of the star) matches the dimmed fraction: newly formed, energy-balanced circumstellar dust around an apparently main-sequence K dwarf that was photospheric in 2010. Most likely collision/disintegration debris; the near-isotropic covering this implies is unusual, so some weight stays on other causes.

discriminating_test: Compare Gaia G epoch residuals of nearby stars of similar magnitude and colour on the same scans for a shared 0.3% depression over days 325-880, and check G flux against scan angle; a shared or scan-angle-dependent signal makes it instrumental, while its absence plus a 25 d rotation signal in TESS/ZTF supports spot activity.

evidence.feature: abbe 1.13, slope_z 0.31, s_fade only 4.63: noise-like visit means
rep_period 25.3 d on a K5-K7 dwarf (bp_rp 1.63, M_G~7)
Within-visit FoV1/FoV2 offsets of 0.7-0.9% that change sign (t=0 FoV2 low; t=960, 973 FoV2 high)
BP depth -0.010+-0.015, RP depth -0.0044+-0.0045: no dimming seen outside G
No IR excess (Ks-W1 0.1, W3/W4 upper limits), NEOWISE W1/W2 change consistent with zero

explanation: A marginal (3.9 sigma) 0.34% G-only depression over 555 days on a quiet K5-K7 dwarf (M_G~7, G-Ks 2.8, no IR excess). Abbe 1.13 says the visit means behave like noise, not a smooth fade. In-dip visits scatter from 0.990 to 1.008, much like the out-of-dip visits (t=0 visit 0.996). Within-visit FoV differences of about 0.7-0.9% change sign between visits, a sign of excess systematic scatter at the same level as the dip. BP and RP show no matching dimming (both nominally brighten; RP is 1.7 sigma from grey), and NEOWISE and ZTF are flat. The most likely causes are low-level activity or spot evolution on the dwarf (the 25 d repeat fits K-dwarf rotation) or residual Gaia calibration effects, with look-elsewhere inflating significance.

discriminating_test: Fold an archival ZTF (or TESS) light curve on P = 87.6-88.6 d. Look for a 2.7% dip lasting 9-11 d at t ~ 128-137 + 88k, and check whether its depth and shape repeat (eclipse or disk) or vary (debris). In the same step, check the Gaia scan angles of the dip transits against the normal ones.

evidence.feature: Bimodal G flux: ~1.000 +/- 0.003 out of dip and 0.968-0.984 in dip, with uniform ~2.7% depth in all three events
Dip lasts from 129.98 to about 137 (at least 6.8 d) on a ~1.5 Rsun dwarf; t~2R/v gives v of about 4 km/s, which cannot recur within 262 d
A period near 88 d with a ~10 d window fits the 392 and 928 dips and misses all 35 normal epochs (pipeline rep_period 87.6 d)
Egress from 0.977 to 0.984 within 0.25 d, consistent with ~2R/v of about 0.44 d at the 88-d orbital speed
RP dims as much as G (~2.9% vs ~2.5%) and both FoVs agree in every in-dip group
BP depth ~1.5 +/- 0.6%, not deeper than RP: grey or reddish, not ISM-like small dust
Low galactic latitude (0-5 deg) and BP scatter twice its errors; scan angles not supplied
ruwe 1.01, ipd_frac_multi_peak 0, normal BP/RP excess: no resolved neighbour or astrometric companion
No WISE photometry, so neither an IR excess nor a waste-heat test is possible

explanation: A quiet star (out-of-dip G scatter ~0.3%) has flat dips of about 2.7% at three times: t=130-137 (8 transits, both FoVs, egress near 136.7), t=392 and t=928. G and RP agree; BP is noisy. A period near 88 d with a 9-11 d window fits every dip and misses every normal epoch. The star is an F/G dwarf (M_G about 4 before extinction; red enough to rule out a giant), so a stellar eclipse lasting 7 d or more is impossible at P~88 d. That would need R1+R2 of about 30 Rsun. The ~0.5 d egress does match a star-sized crossing at the 88-d orbital speed (~55 km/s). This points to an extended, grey occulter in orbit, such as a debris trail or a disk, or else an unphysical or instrumental signal.

discriminating_test: Compare absolute (un-normalised) calibrated photometry from Pan-STARRS or pre-2016 ATLAS with ATLAS or ZTF from 2018 on, or get the Gaia DR4 epoch photometry to 2020. This shows whether the star recovered to its pre-fade level (egress, so a transient occultation) and whether neighbours of similar magnitude and colour share the same G steps (calibration).

evidence.feature: The G deficit persists across about 13 scan groups (t 488-920) in both fov 1 and fov 2
ruwe 0.94, ipd_frac_multi_peak 0, normal BP/RP excess factor 1.21
BP/RP depth ratio 0.967+-0.384 (z_grey -0.09, z_dust -1.9)
Stepwise shape: a plateau at about 0.985 for about 340 d, then a drop to 0.96 at t 865-920, still faint at the last visit
Scatter within the 7-day groups (t 50-58, 431-440) matches the errors, about 0.4%
No IR excess (G-W1 about 1.5); NEOWISE change consistent with grey; 1000 K shell excluded, 300 K shell mildly disfavoured in W2
M_G about 4.5 at 2.6 kpc, |b| 15-20 deg: an old G dwarf or subgiant, not a giant
