explanation: The detected dip is a 0.1% G deficit (3 sigma) spread over only three sparse visits (752, 869, 892 d), and those visits sit inside the scatter of the other visits (days 0, 206 and 376 are lower). BP and RP depths are consistent with zero but have errors 5-7 times the G depth, so the colour test says nothing. slope_z is 1.25, s_fade is 2.0, ZTF g/r/i are flat at the per-cent level and W1/W2 show no change. The 94.9 d repeat rests on a handful of low visits picked out of 22 by a period search. The most likely cause is a noise fluctuation or leftover calibration drift at the 1 mmag level, possibly with small intrinsic microvariability in a reddened F-type star (robust_sigma above the errors). This is not a distinct physical event.

discriminating_test: Fold ZTF g/r at P~232.4 d to get the eclipse profile and g/r depth ratio over all cycles, and check GALEX UV for a hot companion. A smooth, possibly asymmetric, stable chromatic profile with no hot companion favours a dusty circumsecondary disk; a flat-bottomed profile with hot-star colours plus a UV excess favours an eclipse of a hot companion.

evidence.feature: Gaia dips at 455, 675.6, 910.1 and ZTF dips near 1373, 1605, 1837, 2302, 2535, 3000, 3237, 3459, 3697 all fit P~232.4 d (s_rep period 235 d); the gaps that would hold the missing cycles fall in ZTF season gaps
Dip duration ~25-30 d (duty cycle ~12%) for a non-giant star (G=16.6 at 1800 pc, M_G<=5.3, BP-RP 1.37) needs an occulter ~100+ Rsun across at ~40 km/s orbital speed
Chromatic depths: ZTF g ~19%, BP ~13%, G and ZTF r ~10%, RP ~6.5%, ZTF i ~5%; BP/RP depth ratio ~2
Minimum depth stable across ~10 cycles (g minima 0.80-0.84, r minima 0.90-0.915)
Same dips seen in both Gaia fields of view, in G/BP/RP, and in ZTF ~2 arcsec PSF photometry; ruwe 0.99, ipd_frac_multi_peak 0, normal BP/RP excess
No near-IR/mid-IR excess (Ks-W1 0.1, W1-W2 ~-0.1; W3/W4 upper limits only)
Flat, quiet light curve between dips (Gaia G robust sigma 0.5%)
Low galactic latitude (0-5 deg), reddened star, possibly young

explanation: The three Gaia dips (t~455, 676, 910; both fields of view, all bands) are one strictly periodic train. ZTF g/r show nine more dips of ~25-30 d at P~232 d, and extrapolating back lands on Gaia's dips within days (455 falls on egress, so it is shallower). Each reaches a stable ~19% in g, ~10% in r/G and ~5-6% in RP/i. Depth scales roughly as lambda^-3 (BP/RP ~2), which points to small-grain dust or a bluer eclipsed light. The star is an F/G dwarf (M_G<=5.3), so a 25-30 d crossing at ~40 km/s needs an occulter ~0.5 AU across, far larger than any faint star: most likely a dusty circumsecondary disk in a 232 d orbit. A disk confined to the orbit need not show IR excess.

discriminating_test: Run a strict period search (BLS) on the ZTF g/r/i epochs together with the Gaia dip epochs. An eclipsing binary predicts one period of order 0.5-3 d that folds every dip, including the resolved t=1522.5 event, into primary/secondary windows with constant depths. The TESS FFI light curve, if available, should show the same eclipses directly.

evidence.feature: Every Gaia dip is confined to one transit; the companion FOV transit 106.5 min away (157.98, 301.67, 443.23) is normal, so dips last under ~1.8 h
Dips are seen at once in G, BP and RP, and G and RP depths match (e.g. 13.3/12.7%, 25.5/27.3%), so it is a real broadband flux drop
High-cadence ZTF r near t=1522.5 resolves a smooth V-shaped dip from 0.77 down to ~0.66 and back to 0.74 over 41 min, implying a ~1.5-2 h event
Dozens of 20-36% dips in ZTF g, r and i over ~2700 d, single-epoch with normal flux ~1 h before (ztf_i 2194.47 vs 2194.51) and on adjacent nights
Depth up to ~35% on an M-type star (bp_rp 2.49, M_G ~8.8) needs an occulter ~0.6 times the stellar radius, i.e. a star or brown dwarf, not a planet
The 204-day episode (depth 4.1%, 7 visits) is the average of three dipped transits mixed with normal ones; abbe 1.09 and slope_z -0.18 show no smooth fade
ruwe 1.02, ipd_frac_multi_peak 0, and the same dips in 2-arcsec ZTF PSF photometry argue against a neighbour entering the window
NEOWISE W1/W2 show no change and no dust-shell brightening; the colour_of_change ratio is uninformative (ratio_err 2.34)
ztf_g has 10 epochs above 3 sigma (max 1.25), consistent with flares on an active M dwarf

explanation: The flux deficit is not a 204-day fade. It is visit-averaging of three single Gaia transits caught in short, deep dips. Each Gaia dip (10-28%) shows up in one field-of-view transit while the paired transit 106.5 min away is normal. G and RP agree. Dips of this kind recur across Gaia and ZTF g/r/i over ~11 yr, with a ~5-10% duty cycle. One high-cadence ZTF night resolves a dip as a smooth V shape bottoming at ~0.66, lasting ~1.5-2 h. Short, deep (up to ~35%), roughly grey, recurring V-shaped dips on a red M-type star point to a short-period (~day) eclipsing binary with a stellar companion. The g-band brightenings suggest an active, flaring M dwarf.

discriminating_test: Take an optical spectrum (or check OGLE/Be-star and SMC catalogues) for Balmer H-alpha emission and an SMC-like radial velocity (~+150 km/s); emission plus SMC velocity confirms a Be star, while broad quasar lines at a redshift would move the probability to extragalactic.

evidence.feature: bp_rp -0.134 with G-W1 ~0.7 and W1-W2 0.5: hot photosphere plus near-IR excess, far bluer than the quasar locus (G-W1 ~3)
parallax_snr -1.5 with ruwe 0.957: clean astrometry, source must be distant and luminous (or extragalactic), not a nearby CV or white dwarf
W1 visit at t=618 at 0.815+-0.036 coincides with the G minimum (~0.92) and is deeper than G; W1 recovers with G after t~790
Coherent same-sign G, BP and RP changes of 2-6% between FoV pairs 106 min apart (t=531, 662, 734), with both signs across epochs, so no fixed FoV offset
Non-monotonic red-noise light curve (1.11 -> 0.92 -> 1.00 -> 0.93 -> 1.00), abbe 0.28, near-grey depth ratio 1.12+-0.51
ztf_after has no bands (no ZTF epochs), pointing to a far-southern field, consistent with the SMC at |beta|~65, |b|~45

explanation: Most likely a classical Be star, probably in the SMC. The source is blue (BP-RP -0.13) yet has a clear infrared excess (G-W1 0.7, W1-W2 0.5), typical of free-free emission from a decretion disk. No parallax is detected, so it is luminous (M_G near -2 at SMC distance), consistent with |beta| 60-70, |b| 45-50 and no ZTF coverage. It varies stochastically: a near-grey ~10% fade and partial recovery over hundreds of days (abbe 0.28, not monotonic), with W1 fading more than G near the minimum, as disk dissipation predicts, plus coherent 2-6% G/BP/RP changes within 106-min FoV pairs, like Be pulsation. The 'trend' is one phase of disk variability, not an occultation. Quasar colours do not fit.

discriminating_test: ZTF g/r light curves from 2018 on: a rotation period with an approximately 1% spot amplitude and continued slow drift (deeper in g than r) would confirm activity; a flat ZTF level, or a matching G drift in nearby stars of similar magnitude and colour, would point to Gaia calibration.

However, BP (-1.2+/-1.4%) and RP (0.5+/-0.5%) do not reproduce the G depth (about 2 sigma tension), and BP has positive outliers, so residual calibration drift or crowding stays plausible. The data are too thin for strong conclusions.

explanation: Most likely a quasar showing ordinary stochastic AGN variability. The source is faint (G 18.8), blue (BP-RP 0.52), at high galactic latitude, with parallax consistent with zero, and its WISE colours are AGN-like rather than stellar: W1-W2 = 1.2 and W2-W3 = 2.6, with G-W1 about 3.1, far above an F-type photosphere. The G light curve is a smooth red-noise wander (abbe 0.10): about 27% above median at the start, down to about 0.91 at day 733, then back near 1.0, with a bump around day 447. Both fields of view agree, which argues against a scan-angle artefact. The BP/RP ratio (1.22 +/- 0.71) cannot be told apart from grey or 'bluer when brighter'. NEOWISE shows no matching dimming, consistent with a lagged or diluted torus response. W1 also varies over the decade.

A recurring flat-bottomed ~8% fade with sharp edges and stable colour would favour occultation by a companion's disk. A short rotation period with a wandering mean level and spot amplitude that tracks the dim state would confirm magnetic activity.

Fast intra-day changes of 5-8% (t~460, 984, 994) and visit noise of 2.2% against 0.9% errors mark an active, probably fast-rotating star. Against spots, the fade is box-like: ingress under 20 d, a roughly flat floor, and a near-baseline level at the final visit, which fits occultation by a companion's disk. Both FoVs and all bands fade together, and ruwe and excess are normal, so artefacts are unlikely. Without IR or other-survey data, a dust occulter stays untested.

explanation: The trend is really a step: G sits about 2-3% high over days 0-221, then flat near 0.99-1.00, with one low point at day 921. The star is faint (G 16.9) and at low galactic latitude. A high BP/RP excess (about 1.45 against about 1.27 expected) points to a neighbour in the windows. BP and RP jump by 20-35% on single transits that G does not follow, and G changes by up to 5% within 106-min FoV pairs, much more than its errors. So the photometry is visibly contaminated, and the colour test is uninformative. The high state does not alternate between visibility windows, which weakens a simple scan-angle blend. Most likely: a crowding or calibration artefact, or ordinary slow low-amplitude variability of a distant reddened star.

Recovery or recurrence with dust-like colour and no infrared excess points to an occultation by a long-period companion's disk. No change in ZTF points to a Gaia artefact.

explanation: Most likely a slow dust occultation, e.g. by a circumsecondary disk or a dust structure crossing an otherwise quiet F/G dwarf (M_G about 4 at 1.8 kpc, ruwe 1.03). G stays flat to about 0.3% for 700 d. Then it declines gradually: 0.99 at 785 d, 0.947 at 879 d, 0.930 at 900 d, then a 0.928 plateau. The fade shows in both fields of view and in BP, G and RP. Its colour is dust-like (BP/RP 1.57, G/RP about 1.36, z_dust -0.3) but not strongly constrained. An ingress of about 100 d rules out a sharp-edged stellar eclipse (implied speed under 1 km/s), so the occulter must be diffuse or extended. There are no WISE or NEOWISE data to test re-emission. Star cooling or instrumental drift is possible but less likely.

discriminating_test: Take one optical spectrum (H-alpha/Ca II emission and Li 6708 show whether the star is active or young) and compare it with the g-r colour slope of the 2022-25 ZTF fade. Cooling/spots give a small reddening with chromospheric emission; dust gives A_g/A_r about 1.4 with no activity signal.

explanation: The detected dip is a smooth secular fade (about 4% over 964 d, slope -1.5%/yr, abbe 0.08) seen in G and RP, not a discrete dip. The fade is not grey: W1 stays flat, ruling out an opaque occulter, and the colour matches either dust or a temperature/spot change. The likeliest causes are an activity-cycle change in spot coverage on a star above the main sequence (it may be young; there is a flare-like ZTF r event) or slowly changing dust extinction in the plane (W1 slightly favours dust). Residual Gaia calibration drift remains possible.

discriminating_test: Get a multi-year archival ZTF/ATLAS light curve (or one spectrum covering Ca II H&K and H-alpha). If the 1-3% slow, irregular wander continues, with a ~weeks rotation signal or chromospheric emission, it is intrinsic activity. If the baseline is flat apart from one dimming, an occultation or artefact becomes more likely.

The bright hump above baseline after the dip argues against an occultation of a constant star. Both fields of view agree, and the pattern does not repeat at one year, so scan-angle blending is unlikely; ruwe and ipd are clean. Visit-to-visit scatter (0.47%) is three times the errors, so the star is also variable on short timescales. With modest extinction it is a G-type subgiant (M_G about 2-2.5), so spot or activity-cycle variability is most likely, with other low-amplitude intrinsic variability next.

explanation: The 'dip' is a G-only step: the first 25 epochs (t=0-246) sit near 1.03 in both fields of view, all later ones near 1.00, then drift to about 0.99. The G passband is covered by BP and RP, so any real change on the star (occultation, dust, cooling, spots) has to show in at least one of them, and here it is ruled out at more than 8 sigma. Nothing suggests a neighbour (ruwe 1.03, no multi-peak, normal excess factor), NEOWISE is flat apart from one noisy W1 visit, and ZTF is flat. Most likely a residual G calibration or processing offset across a calibration epoch.

explanation: This is most likely a large-amplitude pulsator (RRab, HADS or a short-period Cepheid) sampled at random phases. G reaches 1.85x the median and changes by 25-30% within hours, for example from 1.35 to 1.05 in 4 h at t=970. BP swings much more than RP, so the star is hotter when brighter. The paired transits nearly all fall in time order, whatever the field of view, and the fluxes later in time are lower, which fits a sawtooth light curve that spends most of each cycle declining. The 561-day 'drop' is a sampling effect: of the 16 visit means, two caught near-maximum light before t=409, which pushed up the outside median. The BP/RP depth ratio of 2.35+-0.84 fits a change in temperature. Nothing occults this star.

explanation: Most likely a quasar/AGN showing stochastic red-noise variability. The source is faint (G=20.1), point-like (ruwe 0.99, no multi-peak), has no detectable parallax (snr -1.6), and has a quasar-like optical colour (BP-RP 0.86). Its WISE colours are strongly AGN-like (W1-W2=1.2, W2-W3=3.1) with a mid-IR excess far above any photosphere (G-W1=4.0). The Gaia 'trend' (a 40% fade over 2.7 yr) is one segment of slow variability that ZTF continues over 7 years: low, then bright, then faint, then recovering. The g amplitude exceeds the r amplitude (bluer when brighter), and the change is smooth (abbe 0.08). Independent PSF photometry rules out an instrumental cause, and the parallax argues against a nearby YSO.

discriminating_test: Extract the TESS (or ZTF) light curve to look for a few-day rotation period with percent-level, blue-deeper amplitude, and check an activity indicator (X-ray/GALEX UV or Ca II H&K). Strong rotational modulation plus activity would confirm spots; a quiet star would point back to dust or a blend.

Both fields of view agree within each pair. The deepest epochs are clearly redder (BP about 3.3%, RP about 2.0%), which matches cool spots or a cooler star, and the W1/W2 trends are consistent with that. The most likely cause is rotational spot modulation on an active star, with spot coverage increasing (an activity-cycle-like trend) rather than a smooth fade.

discriminating_test: Run a BLS or phase-dispersion period search on the ~666 ZTF r epochs together with the Gaia epochs: a single strict period that folds every faint epoch into a primary eclipse (~45% deep) and a secondary eclipse would confirm the EB. Also check VSX/ATLAS/ZTF EB catalogues at this position.

explanation: A detached (Algol-type) eclipsing binary, probably a short period of a few days. The flux sits flat at 1.0 and never brightens. Brief dips last under about 10 h: at t=223.39 the flux is 0.66, then 0.97 1.8 h later, and the pair at 986.6-987.0 is 1.00, 0.67, 0.72, 1.00. Dips show in both fields of view, and G, BP and RP dim by the same amount at every epoch (ratio 0.94+-0.18, which rules out dust). ZTF g, r and i show the same fixed floor near 0.53-0.57, as Gaia does (0.56). Two depth levels (about 0.56 and about 0.66-0.84) fit primary and secondary eclipses or partial phases. The 113-d 'episode' is just three visits that happened to land in eclipses, not a real slow fade.

Also correlate the G residuals with scan angle to measure how much the neighbour contributes.

Erratic BP (0.49-1.96) and isolated RP outlier 2.49 at t=195.74 fov 2

explanation: A heavily reddened cool giant in the Galactic plane (BP-RP 3.9, G-Ks 7.8, photospheric W1-W4 with W1-W2 < 0, so no warm dust excess) showing slow semi-regular or long-secondary-period variability. G fades by ~0.25 over 2.6 years with ups and downs and a partial recovery at the end. RP fades less than G, and W2 barely changes (-0.015+/-0.008/yr against -0.093 for grey blocking), which fits the star's own temperature change, not an occulter. On top of this, heavy blending (BP/RP excess 2.48, ipd_frac_multi_peak 24%, ruwe 1.46, 5-10% jumps within hours between fields of view, wild BP, a single RP outlier) adds instrumental scatter. It may also bias part of the trend.

discriminating_test: Compare the per-CCD G fluxes, scan angles and window positions of the t=34.1 and t=128.7 transits with nearby stars of similar magnitude observed in the same transits. If they share the offset, it is calibration. If the offset tracks the scan angle toward a neighbour in a deep image, it is a blend. If neither, check ground-based photometry for real activity.

evidence.feature: Detected drop is set by only two bright single-FOV (fov 1) G epochs at t=34.1 and 128.7 (+1.35%, +1.29%); t=0 pair normal; flat after t=149
colour_of_change: BP and RP depths consistent with zero (0.0014+-0.0055, 0.0005+-0.0062) while G depth is 0.0137+-0.001
Low galactic latitude (0-5 deg), phot_bp_rp_excess_factor 1.27 slightly high for bp_rp 1.33, yet ipd_frac_multi_peak 0 and ruwe 1.01
Star is otherwise quiet: sigma_visit 0.00135, slope_z -1.18, robust_sigma close to errors; no recurrence of a 1.3% feature
No IR excess (Ks 14.1, W1 14.0, W2 14.2; W3/W4 upper limits); NEOWISE changes within noise
Brightening, not dimming, with a non-monotonic shape (t=0 normal, t=34-129 bright, then normal): not a clean step or eclipse
Large in-pair FOV1/FOV2 differences of up to about 0.9% (e.g. t=408.9, 226.5, 907.4) suggest the quoted G errors are underestimated, with non-Gaussian outliers

explanation: The 'drop' is not a dimming. It comes from two isolated single-FOV G transits (t=34, t=129) about 1.3% bright. The t=0 FOV pair is normal, and every epoch after t=149 is flat to about 0.1% for roughly 800 days. BP and RP show no change (depths 0.1+-0.5% and 0.05+-0.6%; at those epochs about 0.5% against the expected 1.3%). That mildly favours a G-only instrumental cause, such as an early-mission calibration or processing offset or a CCD defect. A neighbour entering the window at certain scan angles is plausible in this low-latitude field (BP/RP excess slightly high), but it should contaminate BP and RP more. There is no IR excess, NEOWISE is uninformative, and there are no ZTF or TESS data. A real brightening episode (activity) is possible on an otherwise quiet dwarf.

discriminating_test: Check ZTF and TESS photometry of this star for a rotation period of days to weeks with a percent-level amplitude that varies over seasons (which confirms spots and an activity cycle), and compare the Gaia G trend with nearby stars of similar magnitude and colour to rule out residual calibration drift.

evidence.feature: Month-scale wandering of about 0.5-1% superposed on the decline, not a clean linear trend (abbe 0.55)
Absolute G about 5-6 at bp_rp 1.21: a main-sequence G/K star, not a giant
FoV 1 and FoV 2 agree within transit pairs during the low state (611, 674, 989 d)
BP and RP both show the 610-735 d low; ratio 0.92 +/- 0.62 is unconstrained
Galactic latitude 0-5 deg, but ruwe 0.94, ipd_frac_multi_peak 0 and normal BP/RP excess
W1-W2 = -0.1 and no strong excess (Ks-W1 0.3)
Only 27 visits with correlated variability inflate slope_z, and residual Gaia drift at the 1% level is possible
No recurrence and a multi-year timescale

explanation: A G/K dwarf (M_G about 5-6 after modest plane extinction) that is otherwise variable at the 0.4% level (robust_sigma 0.0042 against 0.0011 errors) shows a 1.2% decline over 990 d. The decline is not smooth: G stays near 1.003 until about 550 d, then wanders between 0.987 and 1.000 on timescales of weeks (710 d low, 774 d recovery, 853-886 d low, 947 d high), and BP and RP follow it. Both fields of view agree within a transit pair, the colour ratio is consistent with grey or with cooling (0.92 +/- 0.62), and WISE cannot discriminate. The most likely cause is spot evolution or an activity cycle on an active star, sampled sparsely. Residual calibration drift or crowding in the plane are the main alternatives.

discriminating_test: Run a periodogram on the ZTF/TESS photometry for a few-day rotation period. Also check whether g-r slightly reddens as the star fades, and whether a chromospheric activity index is high. A short rotation period with strong activity would confirm a spot cycle. A grey fade with no rotation signal would raise disk occultation or instrumental causes.

evidence.feature: Smooth G trend -0.58%/yr, slope_z -4.5, abbe 0.37; all visits after t=490 lie below the early ones
ZTF g and r both fade 3-5% over 2018-2022 and then level off (change after 2020: g -2.9%, r -3.2%), gradually across seasons in both filters
ZTF g/r fade ratio ~0.9-1.1, matching cool-spot contrast on a K dwarf, not the ~1.4 of interstellar-like dust
~1% rise within 2-3 days in both dense Gaia groups (t 128-131 and 311-314), shared by fov 1 and 2
M_G ~5.5 with BP-RP 1.34 (a main-sequence K star), not a giant
ruwe 1.03, ipd_frac_multi_peak 0, normal BP/RP excess factor
W1-W2 0.1 (photospheric); W3 11.8 is near the AllWISE detection limit at low latitude, so it is unreliable; no ir_excess_sigma given
Gaia BP/RP ratio 1.04 +/- 3.36 and NEOWISE slopes have errors far larger than the signal

explanation: This is an active, spotted K dwarf (M_G ~5.5, BP-RP 1.34 at 990 pc) whose activity cycle slowly changes how much of the surface spots cover. Gaia G fades by ~1.4% over 923 d, and that is real: every late visit sits below the early ones. ZTF, an independent survey, confirms slow multi-year changes. Both g and r fade by ~4-5% between 2018 and 2022 and then level off. The g/r depth ratio is ~0.9-1.1, which is what cool spots on a ~4700 K star give (~1.1). Interstellar-like dust would give ~1.4. Both dense Gaia groups show ~1% changes within 2-3 days, consistent with rotating spots. Astrometry and blending indicators are clean. BP/RP and NEOWISE cannot tell the options apart.

discriminating_test: Get an archival optical spectrum (SDSS/DESI/LAMOST) to check for broad emission lines at a cosmological redshift, or the ZTF light curve to check for continued aperiodic stochastic variability.

evidence.feature: W1-W2 = 1.2 mag, W1-W3 = 4.0 mag (AGN mid-IR colours)
parallax_snr 1.3 at G = 19, |b| 35-40 deg, bp_rp 0.47
smooth monotonic G rise 0.83 -> 1.46 over 978 d, abbe 0.055, slope 21%/yr; dip is just the early low state
fov 1 and fov 2 agree within errors at every paired transit
W1 NEOWISE flux also trends upward by ~30% over the decade
ruwe 1.01, ipd_frac_multi_peak 0, bp_rp_excess 1.18: isolated point source
rep_period 27.7 d from only 18 visits; one long low state, not repeating eclipses

explanation: This is most likely a quasar, and the 'dip' is just the faint start of a smooth, red-noise brightening. WISE colours W1-W2 = 1.2 and W1-W3 = 4.0 sit squarely in the AGN locus. The source is faint and blue (G = 19, BP-RP 0.47), at high galactic latitude, with parallax consistent with zero (SNR 1.3), and ruwe 1.01 says it is point-like. G rises monotonically from 0.83 to 1.46 over 978 d (abbe 0.055, slope_z 10, both fields of view agree), so the first three visits fall below the median. W1 brightens on the same timescale. The 27.7 d 'repeat' rests on only 18 visits and is not credible. BP/RP depths (ratio 1.0 +/- 1.06) carry no information.

discriminating_test: Check whether the G and RP fluxes of each transit correlate with scan angle, especially for the bright early visits. If they do, the trend comes from a crowding neighbour. If they do not, a multi-season red or near-IR light curve (ZTF i or VVV Ks) should show semi-regular cycles.

evidence.feature: G-Ks ~9.7, BP-RP 4.38, Ks 8.98, galactic plane, parallax_snr 0.11: distant, heavily extincted luminous red giant
Trend driven by non-monotonic bright early visits (1.51, 1.08, 1.31, 1.24) then plateau; abbe 0.44
RP also fades (depth 0.18 vs G 0.34), consistent with larger amplitude at shorter wavelength
NEOWISE W2 slope -0.009+/-0.009 per yr vs grey prediction -0.129
No mid-IR excess (Ks-W1 0.33, W1-W2 0.05, W3 not bright)
G transit pairs 106 min apart differ by up to ~15% (e.g. t=575, 966) against 1-2% errors; phot_bp_rp_excess_factor 2.29; BP wildly scattered
G bright at t=219.7 (1.24) while RP at the same time is 0.97: G and RP poorly correlated per epoch
Colour ratio 26.5+/-22 from noise-dominated BP: uninformative

explanation: This is most likely a distant, heavily reddened luminous red giant (G-Ks about 9.7, BP-RP 4.4, |b|<5 deg, parallax insignificant, Ks about 9), and nearly all such stars are semi-regular or irregular variables. A few bright early visits (0-220 d) drive the 'trend', after which the flux sits near the median. The change is not monotonic (1.51, 1.08, 1.31...), and an Abbe value of 0.44 fits undersampled long-period variability. RP also declines, but less, as expected for a cool pulsator. A flat W2 rules out grey blocking. The lack of any IR excess argues against RCB, YSO or disk dust. BP is dominated by noise, so the colour test says nothing. Pairs of field-of-view transits 106 min apart differ by about 15%, which shows crowding noise, so a blend contribution is the main alternative.

discriminating_test: Split the ZTF g, r and i light curves by field and CCD and fit each slope separately, and add a Ca II H&K or H-alpha activity measurement. If every band fades at the same rate, the fade is grey (an occulter or an injection). If g truly fades less than i and W1, the colour change is opposite to dust and spots. A strong activity cycle would favour spots.

evidence.feature: Same slow fade in Gaia G, ZTF r/i and NEOWISE W1 over ~11 yr
BP/RP depth ratio 1.01 +/- 0.63 and W1 slope -0.0139 +/- 0.0071 vs grey prediction -0.0065
W1 fades about as much as or more than G; dust predicts -0.0005, star cooling -0.0018
ZTF g fades less (about -0.3%/yr) than r and i; spots and dust would dim g most
Quiet star otherwise: sigma_visit 0.28%, close to the photometric errors, so no rotational modulation
No IR excess (Ks-W1 0.2, W1-W2 0.1), high galactic latitude, main-sequence luminosity
ruwe 0.98, ipd_frac_multi_peak 0, normal BP/RP excess
parallax_snr 46 at 400 pc gives a dwarf

explanation: A quiet K7/M0 dwarf (M_G~8.1, no IR excess, ruwe 0.98, C* ~0) fades steadily and smoothly by about 0.6-1%/yr. Several independent instruments show it: Gaia G (-0.65%/yr), BP and RP alike (ratio 1.01), ZTF r and i season means (about -0.6 and -0.85%/yr over 7 yr) and NEOWISE W1 (about -1%/yr over 10 yr). Because the instruments agree, a Gaia artefact is unlikely. The fade is grey or slightly deeper in the red. Dust or a cooling star would dim W1 far less, and a spot cycle would dim g most, yet g dims least. The only listed process that fits naturally is an optically thick occulter on our sightline that grows slowly (disk-like). Otherwise this is a fade with no clear known cause, possibly injected.

discriminating_test: Pull archival photometry from another survey that overlaps the Gaia fade (t about 500-950), such as ATLAS, Pan-STARRS or CRTS. A matching 1-3% fade there, deeper in bluer bands, confirms the star itself varied. A flat light curve shows a G-only artefact or injection.

evidence.feature: Smooth 1.8% G fade lasting at least 380 d, with partial recovery, seen in both FoV 1 and FoV 2
ZTF g shows a multi-season swing of a few percent, larger than r and i (activity-cycle-like chromaticity)
BP depth -0.007+/-0.019 and RP depth -0.0067+/-0.0097 against a G depth of 0.0176+/-0.0015: G does not equal the BP/RP combination at about 2.5-2.7 sigma
Fade is coherent in time across scan groups rather than scattered by group; ipd_frac_multi_peak 0; BP/RP excess normal for its colour
Ks-W1 about 0.2, W1-W2 about 0, W3/W4 upper limits: a bare photosphere, no warm dust
Parallax SNR 13 with stellar W1-W2 colour
NEOWISE W1 change -0.012+/-0.026 is consistent with every model

explanation: The most likely cause is slow intrinsic variability of a K5-ish dwarf (M_G about 6.8, no IR excess, ruwe about 1), such as a spot/activity-cycle swing, with a G-specific calibration drift a close second. G fades 1.8% (11 sigma) from about t=500, smoothly in time and in both fields of view, with only partial recovery by t=949. That pattern is not scan-angle or group-like, and a 380 d shallow event that never recurs is not an eclipse. ZTF 2018-2025 shows multi-season wander of a few percent, larger in g than in r and i, as an activity cycle would. Against it: BP and RP show no fade (-0.7+/-1.9%, -0.7+/-1.0%), about 2.5 sigma off any change on the star, which favours a G-only artefact or a G-only injection.

discriminating_test: Check absolute-calibrated archival photometry (Pan-STARRS, ATLAS or ASAS-SN) for 2015-2019 to confirm the 2% fade outside Gaia, measure when and how the star recovered before ZTF, and see whether its colour stays grey. Add a Ca II H&K activity spectrum to test the magnetic-cycle option.

evidence.feature: Fade present in both fov 1 and fov 2 at days 623-956
BP and RP medians also drop about 1.5-2% after day 623, roughly grey within large errors
Smooth, slow decline over the whole Gaia span (abbe 0.22, slope_z -8.2) with small sigma_visit 0.0032
Absolute magnitude about 5.3 with BP-RP 1.08: K dwarf, not an evolved star
W3/W4 upper limits only, Ks-W1 near photospheric; NEOWISE change rules out a 1000 K shell
Dip lasts more than 332 days with gradual ingress and only 2% depth
ruwe 0.985 and ipd_frac_multi_peak 0: no sign of a close neighbour
ZTF flat from 2018 to 2023 (g change +0.4%, r -0.02%), so the fade did not continue later
Parallax SNR 8.5 and stellar colours

explanation: A quiet main-sequence G8-K1 dwarf (M_G about 5.3, ruwe 0.985, no multi-peak) shows a smooth G decline: about 1.009 early, 0.995 by day 555, then about 0.982 from day 623 to the last visit. The decline appears in both fields of view, and the BP and RP medians drop by a similar 1.5-2%, so a G-only calibration fault or an FOV offset is unlikely. The colour ratio has no constraining power (error 1.5), and NEOWISE's 4% errors only rule out a hot 1000 K shell. The visit-to-visit noise of 0.3% argues against a strongly spotted active star, so a long grey occultation by a slow disk or dust structure is the leading natural option. ZTF was flat in 2018-2023, so no fade recurred later. A magnetic-cycle brightness change or residual Gaia processing remains possible.

discriminating_test: Take a new spectrum and compare it with an archival one (or Gaia epoch XP spectra over time). Check whether the fade follows an extinction curve, with deeper Na D or DIBs and unchanged line ratios, or a drop in Teff. Also check whether NEOWISE W1 for nearby field stars of similar brightness shows the same drift.

evidence.feature: Linear G fade -0.79%/yr, slope_z -17, abbe 0.08 (smooth)
ZTF g and r continue the same fade for ~7 yr after Gaia; Gaia, ZTF and NEOWISE all agree
ZTF g fades faster than r (ratio ~1.3-1.5): redder when fainter
NEOWISE W1 slope ~ -0.5%/yr, ~0.6 of G, far above the dust-in-front prediction
Short-timescale quiet star (sigma_visit 0.0017, stable within 3-4 day clusters): no rotational modulation
No IR excess (Ks-W1=0, W1-W2=0), F/G turnoff star 600 pc from plane
ruwe 0.98, ipd_frac_multi_peak 0, normal BP/RP excess
Parallax SNR 15 and W1-W2=0
Gaia BP/RP depth ratio 2.76 +/- 2.33 is uninformative

explanation: The 'dip' is a smooth secular fade, not a discrete event: Gaia G falls about 0.8-0.9%/yr (slope_z -17) and ZTF continues it at the same rate for 7 more years (g about 1.1%/yr, r about 0.75%/yr), roughly 10% total. Three independent instruments agreeing rules out most artefacts. The star reddens as it fades (g/r about 1.3-1.5), which fits dust or a cooler star. But NEOWISE W1 also fades, about 0.5 +/- 0.17%/yr (about 0.6 of G), which fits the star changing itself (spots or temperature) better than dust in front (predicted about 0.05 of G). However, this F/G turnoff star at 2.1 kpc is very quiet on short timescales (sigma_visit 0.17%) and has no IR excess, so a decade-long activity-cycle fade this large is hard to explain.

discriminating_test: Get the per-transit scan angles and check whether the bright G epochs cluster at one scan angle, then look in deeper high-resolution imaging (e.g. Pan-STARRS/DECaPS) for a resolved neighbour within ~2 arcsec at that position angle.

evidence.feature: ruwe 9.0, ipd_frac_multi_peak 4, phot_bp_rp_excess_factor 1.99, parallax_snr -1.5, |b| 0-5 deg
G brightenings up to 1.6 at several epochs (e.g. t=278.3/278.5, 559.8/559.9) with BP and RP near 1.0 at the same epochs
Detected 'drop' is the outside-window median raised by the bright contaminated epochs; normal G epochs stay near 0.98-1.0 throughout
G depth 0.0121 +/- 0.0196, consistent with zero; slope_z -1.8
BP low (~0.88-0.93) at t=843-899 while G is flat and RP scatters by ~8% between paired transits 106 min apart
NEOWISE W1/W2 change consistent with zero; no IR context for a dust excess

explanation: A crowding artefact. The source sits in the Galactic plane with ruwe 9, ipd_frac_multi_peak 4, BP/RP excess factor 1.99 and a negative parallax, all signs of an unresolved neighbour. G has repeated brightenings of 17-60% (t=0-1.3, 92, 180, 278, 370, 560), seen in both fields of view at once but absent in BP and RP. That fits a neighbour entering the small G window at some scan angles, while the larger BP/RP windows always hold its flux. The 'drop, bright at first and fainter afterwards' comes from those early bright epochs against a flat baseline near 0.98-1.0. The G depth (0.012 +/- 0.020) is not significant, the colour ratio is unconstrained (2.35 +/- 2.11), and W1/W2 show no change.

discriminating_test: Get Gaia DR4 epoch photometry (to 2020) for this star and for same-magnitude, same-colour stars on the same transits. If the late low G points are shared, or reverse with no RP counterpart, the cause is instrumental. If the star keeps fading coherently in G and RP and then flattens to meet ZTF, it is the star's own activity.

evidence.feature: G trend (slope_z -4.56, 16 visits) driven by last 3-4 low single-transit fov-2 visits (751-937 d), last one 0.967
RP depth -0.013+/-0.023 versus G depth 0.035+/-0.008 for a red star whose G flux is RP-dominated
ZTF g and r flat after 2020 versus 2018-2019 (change +0.4%, +0.1%; slopes ~0)
NEOWISE W1 slope +1.8+/-1.4%/yr versus grey prediction -1.4%/yr
bp_rp 2.17, M_G ~8.1 at 1 kpc, W1-W2 = 0, G-Ks ~3.2: early-M dwarf photosphere
ruwe 0.975, ipd_frac_multi_peak 0, |b| 40-45 deg
No IR excess (W1-W2 ~0, W3/W4 upper limits)
Dense 516-519 d sequence quiet at noise level; abbe 0.376 indicates only slow structure

explanation: This is a faint (G=18.1) early-M dwarf: bp_rp 2.17, M_G about 8, W1-W2 = 0, no IR excess. G fades by a low-significance 3.5% over 937 d, and most of that comes from the last three single fov-2 transits. RP shows no matching fade (-1.3+/-2.3%, where about 2.5-3.5% is expected), and BP is too noisy to say anything. NEOWISE W1 disfavours grey blocking, and ZTF g/r stay flat from 2018 to 2025, so the fade did not continue. The likeliest causes are a leftover Gaia G calibration or processing drift for a faint red source, or slow changes in the star's spot coverage (an activity cycle). There is no sign of any occulter.

discriminating_test: Search TESS/ZTF for a rotation period of a few days and check the spot amplitude, then use an absolutely calibrated multi-year light curve (ASAS-SN or ZTF without per-field normalisation) to see whether the 5-10% slow change repeats as an activity cycle with redder-when-fainter colour; also check Gaia epoch scan angles to rule out a blend.

evidence.feature: sigma_visit 0.0194 against G errors of about 0.003; ZTF r night means change 4-8% between nights (3789-3793) against 1.4% errors
G not monotonic: brightens to 1.04-1.055 at days 183-357, back near 1.0 at days 385-562, then 0.95-0.97 at days 733-960 (abbe 0.35)
Depths BP 0.112, G 0.070, RP 0.049; ratio 2.3 +/- 0.97 (z_grey 1.34, z_dust 0.62), so the dimming is reddening, as cooler spots or dust produce
NEOWISE W1 slope -0.002 +/- 0.016 /yr, against -0.026 predicted for grey blocking; consistent with a temperature change or dust in front
ruwe 0.93, ipd_frac_multi_peak 0, phot_bp_rp_excess_factor 1.37 (about normal for this colour)
Differences between the two field-of-view transits within a visit change sign from visit to visit (no consistent FoV1/FoV2 offset)
M_G about 7.1 before extinction with BP-RP 2.16: a dwarf, overluminous for an unreddened early M star (young or binary), at galactic latitude 5-10 deg
Near-photospheric infrared colours (Ks-W1 0.2, W1-W2 0.1; W3 near its detection limit)
Single-band RP outlier 1.107 at day 765.97 while G is 0.957

explanation: A red (BP-RP 2.16) K/M dwarf at 770 pc that sits above the main sequence, so probably young or a binary, and that varies on its own: 2% visit-to-visit scatter in Gaia and 4-8% night-to-night changes in ZTF, well above the errors. The 'trend' is not a clean fade. G rises to about 1.05 around days 180-360, then falls to about 0.95 by day 960, a roughly 10% slow modulation typical of changing spot coverage or an activity cycle. The dimming is chromatic (BP/RP ratio 2.3 +/- 1.0, as cool spots produce), and NEOWISE W1 stays flat, which disfavours grey blocking. There are no signs of blending (ruwe 0.93, no multi-peak, normal BP/RP excess) and no systematic field-of-view offset. Dust stays possible, but the infrared is close to photospheric.

discriminating_test: Check whether the three bright visits fall before the first Gaia decontamination (Sept 2014) or during the early scanning-law period, and whether nearby stars of similar G and colour observed on the same scans show a matching +3% offset. Also check the scan angles of those visits against later ones.

evidence.feature: Only the first 3 visits (6 transits, t=0-35 d) are high at +2-3%; every later visit is near 1.00 for about 850 d
Excess is present in both fov 1 and fov 2 at every early visit, so it is not an offset between fields of view; it is an offset by epoch
ruwe 0.994 and ipd_frac_multi_peak 0; the RP excess (2.7%) is no larger than G's even though RP has the larger window
G robust_sigma 0.0055 against error 0.0045; ZTF g/r/i robust_sigma equals the errors; the star is otherwise quiet
All three early visits are high by the same amount, which random rotational phases would not produce
NEOWISE W1 change +0.001+-0.013 against a predicted -0.028 for grey blocking; the W2 +0.096 rise is about 2 sigma from noisy visits and W1 does not back it
K dwarf at 1.2 kpc and |b| 35-40 deg, W1-W2 about -0.1 with no excess
BP/RP depth ratio 2.16+-1.22 fits grey, dust and temperature change alike; BP and RP scatter well above their errors

explanation: The 'drop' is really an excess in the first three Gaia visits (t=0-35 d): about +2.8% in G, seen in both fields of view and drifting down. After that the star stays flat to within about 0.5% for 850 days. A change that only touches the opening weeks of the record looks most like a calibration problem from the early mission (the period before decontamination or during the early scanning law) that did not get removed with the shared drift. The star is a quiet K dwarf (M_G about 6.7, BP-RP 1.37) with no infrared excess, ruwe about 1 and no multi-peak images. In ZTF it shows no excess scatter. That makes spots, dust or eclipses unlikely. The colour ratio (2.2+-1.2) tells us nothing either way.

discriminating_test: Check whether the step is shared and whether it persisted. Compare the Gaia epoch G of nearby stars of similar magnitude and colour on the same scans for a step between t=403 and t=496. Also compare zero-pointed absolute photometry (PS1/ZTF/ATLAS, against field comparison stars) with the pre-fade Gaia level, to see whether the 4% deficit is still there after 2018 and whether it is chromatic.

evidence.feature: Same ~3-4% deficit in both fov 1 and fov 2 across 8 visits over 424 d
Abbe 0.077 and slope_z -9.5: smooth, coherent secular fade rather than scatter
Abrupt ~2.8% drop within a 94 d gap, then gradual deepening; otherwise quiet star with no rotational modulation within 4-day visit groups
ruwe 1.08, ipd_frac_multi_peak 0, phot_bp_rp_excess_factor 1.26 normal for bp_rp 1.44
BP/RP depth ratio 2.19+/-2.17 uninformative; RP depth 0.0155+/-0.013 is about 1.7 sigma below G depth
RP robust_sigma 4.5% vs median error 1.7%: excess BP/RP scatter suggests window contamination or poor faint-source photometry
Abs M_G about 7 and G-Ks 2.5 at 1100 pc, ~300 pc off the plane: main-sequence K dwarf, not evolved, unlikely young
424+ d duration with gradual deepening, no recurrence evidence
ZTF 2018-2024 shows no internal change (g -0.15%, r -0.11%), but is self-normalised so cannot test recovery to the pre-fade level

explanation: G is flat (visit noise about 0.3%) for 400 d. Somewhere in the gap between t=403 and t=496 it drops about 2.8%, then keeps fading slowly to about 4.5% by the last visit. Both fields of view show this, so it is not a FOV offset or a one-epoch defect. The source is a reddened K dwarf (M_G about 7, ruwe 1.08, clean BP/RP excess, no multi-peak), so blending looks unlikely. BP/RP are too noisy for a colour (ratio 2.2+/-2.2), and RP's 1.6% looks shallower than G's 3.8%. ZTF is normalised to itself, so it cannot show recovery. No single cause stands out: a magnetic-cycle or spot change, a slow occultation by a disk or dust, or a residual Gaia calibration step are all plausible.

discriminating_test: Plot per-transit G flux against scan angle and check the Gaia neighbour within ~2 arcsec (or ZTF PSF photometry 2018-2020): a scan-angle correlation with a flat ZTF light curve confirms blending; a slow ZTF r/i trend would point to the star's own variability.

evidence.feature: ipd_frac_multi_peak 40, phot_bp_rp_excess_factor 2.84, ruwe 2.01
Isolated huge brightenings in G, BP (195x) and RP (18x) at single transits
At t=841 FoV-2 points ~0.96 vs FoV-1 ~0.99 within hours
Abbe 1.07, slope_z -1.33, only 15 visits; in-window visits at 845-924 are at or above median

Abbe 1.07 means noise-like. BP/RP depths are consistent with zero and tell us nothing. Most likely blending or crowding that changes with scan angle. explanation: A detached eclipsing binary. discriminating_test: Run a period search on the dense ZTF g/r photometry (or the Gaia epochs) for a stable period of hours. Fold the light curve: a pulsation shape with g amplitude well above r would be confirmed. Check that the residuals after removing it show no dip near t=410-580 and no 80.7 d recurrence.

evidence.feature: Consecutive FOV1/FOV2 transits 106.5 min apart differ by 10-13% in G, with the sign alternating between epochs
Pair-difference amplitude BP > G > RP (e.g. t=199.4: 0.20, 0.13, 0.125; t=733.5: 0.16, 0.13, 0.09), so the variation is chromatic
G flux spread is symmetric about 1 (0.934 to 1.080), with no one-sided bright excursions
robust_sigma 0.053 against a median error of 0.0045: intrinsic variability far above the noise on hour timescales
The detected dip has 3 visits, depth 1.6% in G, an inconsistent colour (BP 9%, RP about 0), abbe 1.2 and slope_z 0.56
ruwe 1.05 and ipd_frac_multi_peak 0 show no resolved neighbour or astrometric companion
Large flux swings over hours could also come from a contact binary, though its colour change would be smaller

explanation: A blue (BP-RP 0.49), faint star that varies by about 13% within 106.5 min. The paired FOV transits swing in both directions (FOV1 high at some epochs, FOV2 high at others), so this is not a fixed FOV offset. The amplitude is largest in BP and smallest in RP, which is what a short-period pulsator (delta Scuti/SX Phe/low-amplitude RRc) does when it is hotter at maximum light. The flux values spread symmetrically about 1, as a sinusoid sampled at random phases does. The 'repeat' dip at 80.7 d comes from 19 visit means that each average two random pulsation phases. The in-dip visits sit only 1-2% low, inside that sampling scatter. Abbe 1.2 and slope_z 0.56 show no coherent slow change.

discriminating_test: Get the per-transit Gaia scan angles and check whether the G residuals and the BP/RP excess follow scan angle. Then check a deep PSF image (DECaPS/Pan-STARRS) for a neighbour within about 2 arcsec, and look at ZTF/PS1 PSF photometry for whether the fade is really on the star.

explanation: Most likely a crowding artefact. This faint (G=17.3), red source lies within 5 deg of the Galactic plane and has every blending flag: BP/RP excess 1.84, ruwe 2.59, multi-peak windows, a parallax at -3.6 sigma and no 2MASS/WISE match. RP independently dips 4.7 +/- 1.4% during the episode
BP/RP depth ratio 0.33 +/- 0.62 (z_grey -1.08, z_dust -2.2); cooling would give ratio ~1.4
Single in-dip NEOWISE W1 visit -7.0 +/- 2.8%, closer to grey prediction (-2.3%) than star-temperature (-0.7%) or dust-in-front (~0%); 1000 K shell brightening excluded
ZTF g and r show coherent slow excursions of 2-3% (e.g. r ~1.02-1.03 around days 2718-2773, g/r high around 3890-3965, g ~1.5% low around 2030-2215)

Low visit-to-visit noise (sigma_visit 0.42%) and flat dense 7-day sequence: little rotational modulation
Absolute magnitude places star on dwarf main sequence, not an evolved star

explanation: A quiet main-sequence K dwarf (M_G about 6.5-7, no IR excess) shows one smooth, symmetric fade of about 3.5% at minimum, lasting about 250 d (days 518-808). It is seen in both fields of view and independently in RP, so a single-transit or FoV artefact is unlikely. Within large errors the colour is grey (z_grey -1.1, z_dust -2.2), and the one W1 visit inside the fade also dims. Both fit a large, partly transparent occulter, such as a circumsecondary disk or debris cloud crossing slowly in a wide orbit. Any stellar eclipse would need an impossibly low speed for this duration. The main alternative is the star's own slow variability: ZTF later shows coherent excursions of +/-2-3% lasting months.

discriminating_test: Pull long-baseline ZTF/ATLAS g and r photometry (2018 onward) for this star. Check whether its mean level keeps wandering at a few per cent with colour changes like temperature changes, which would mean activity or spots, or sits flat apart from a single grey fade, which would mean a disk occultation. In the same data, measure the period of the hours-scale modulation.

evidence.feature: Intrinsic ~3% variability on hours timescales (G robust_sigma 0.019 vs flux_err ~0.003), changes of 2-3% between paired transits 106.5 min apart, no FoV offset, persists during the dip
Smooth symmetric fade: baseline ~1.01 early, ~0.99 at 640-700, ~0.97 at 736-898, ~0.99 at 948-956; abbe 0.34; trend flag arises from dip near end of span

explanation: The star varies intrinsically by about 3% within hours (robust_sigma 0.019 against errors of 0.003, seen in both fields of view and during the dip), so it is an active short-period variable: a spotted rapid rotator, a contact binary or a pulsator. The detected dip is a smooth, roughly symmetric fade of about 4% from a baseline near 1.01. It has wings at days 640-700 and 948-956 and a core over days 736-898, which reads as a slow change in mean level. My leading explanation is a change in spot or activity coverage on this active star; its BP/RP ratio of 1.9±0.8 fits that. The single in-dip NEOWISE visit dims grey-like, which points instead to a grey occultation by a circumsecondary disk.

discriminating_test: Run a BLS/phase-dispersion period search on the ~100 ZTF g+r dip epochs together with the Gaia dip times (or on TESS 30-min data). A single strict period of a few days that puts every deep dip into a primary (~40%) and possibly a secondary eclipse window would confirm an eclipsing binary. No such period would bring back dippers or debris.

A detached eclipsing binary with a period of days, sampled at random phases in and out of eclipse, explains the varying depths, the grey colour, the roughly 4% duty cycle and the quiet star between dips.

discriminating_test: Pull the per-CCD G fluxes, scan angles and window or centroid offsets for the transits at t=87, 357 and 615, and check G for nearby stars in the same transits. Flux loss that tracks scan angle or window position, or dips that other stars share, would confirm an instrumental cause.

Since G covers the same wavelengths as BP plus RP, no real dimming of the star can show up in G alone. Whole transit groups being affected, with normal groups days later, points to flux loss in the narrower G window (source near the window edge, a truncated window or poor centring) or a G-only processing fault. Gaia 106.5-min FoV pairs and same-day transits change by 0.15-0.30, e.g. 1.115 to 0.818 in 4 h, 0.806 to 0.956 in 1.8 h
Brightest in-episode G points (1.114, 1.115) equal the out-of-episode maximum (about 1.12), so the episode is phase sampling and no mean flux was lost
BP/RP depth ratio 2.07 +/- 0.60 (z_grey 1.76); BP robust sigma 0.22 vs RP 0.10; ZTF g sigma 0.22 vs r 0.13
Only 16 Gaia visits, sigma_visit much smaller than robust_sigma, rep_period 37.7 d: visit means of a fast variable can drift with the sampling and mimic slow episodes
Large-amplitude fast variability also seen in 2-arcsec ZTF PSF photometry; ipd_frac_multi_peak 0, ruwe 1.1

explanation: This looks like a short-period, large-amplitude pulsator (RR Lyrae or HADS type) that Gaia sampled sparsely. ZTF g swings back and forth between about 0.8 and 1.3, changing by 10-40% within 0.5-3 h, and the values pile up at both extremes. Gaia pairs 106.5 min apart also jump by 0.15-0.30. Gaia fluxes cluster at both extremes overall. Inside the 'episode', Gaia points span the full range, and the brightest ones (1.114, 1.115) equal the brightest outside (1.12). So there is no real drop in the mean: the faint visits just happened to fall at faint phases. The change is strongly chromatic: BP/RP ratio 2.07, ZTF g scatter about 1.7x r. That is what temperature pulsation does, not grey eclipses of a contact binary.

discriminating_test: Run a BLS/strict-period search on the ZTF g+r+i faint epochs together with the Gaia dip times (226.53, 626.52, 786.70). Check that every dip phases onto one or two windows at a fixed depth and duration, and whether there is a secondary eclipse.

High-cadence ZTF r run at t=1576.28-1576.35 flat at ~0.81 for ~1.7 h (flat-bottomed eclipse)
Gaia dips are single transits lasting hours (626.27 normal, 626.52 at 0.81, 626.59 at 0.95)
Dips seen together in G, BP and RP at 626.52 and in ZTF PSF photometry, on another survey and clock
ruwe 0.985, ipd_frac_multi_peak 0, normal BP/RP excess factor 1.24
Roughly 4-5% of epochs in a dip, as expected for a few-hour eclipse in a period of days
No IR excess (Ks-W1 0.3, W1-W2 about -0.5); NEOWISE flat
RP only 0.969 at t=786.70 while G and BP read ~0.83
19% depth on a reddened star, likely K or earlier intrinsically, too deep for most planets

explanation: The 160-d 'dimming episode' (2.4%) is just visit averages pulled down by brief, deep single-transit dips. G falls to 0.81-0.88 at t=226.5, 626.5 and 786.7, with normal transits a few hours either side. At 626.5 it recovers from 0.81 to 0.95 within 106 min. ZTF g, r and i show the same dips again and again from 2018 to 2025, always bottoming out at about 0.78-0.82. About 4-5% of epochs are in a dip, the dips are roughly grey across BP/RP/g/r/i, and the depth does not change, so this is a detached eclipsing binary with eclipses a few hours long. Clean astrometry (ruwe 0.99, no multi-peak) and the ZTF PSF photometry argue the dips come from this star and not a blend.

discriminating_test: Run a period search on the ZTF/ATLAS g and r light curve (2018 onward). A rotation period of a few days with a few-% amplitude and slow changes in mean level would confirm spot variability. A flat light curve would point to a Gaia-specific instrumental or contamination trend.

evidence.feature: G fade 4.8% over 992 d with abbe 0.52 and 2% visit-to-visit scatter beyond the errors
Sharp drop of about 6% at t~834.7, seen in both FOV1 and FOV2, low for more than 1 d, back to 1.017 by t=898
bp_rp 1.71, G-Ks 3.2, parallax SNR 3.3: probably an early-M dwarf, not a distant giant
W1-W2 about -0.1, Ks-W1 near 0, W3/W4 only upper limits: no warm dust or AGN colours
W1-W2 not red, ruwe 1.0, normal BP/RP excess factor: point-like stellar source
BP and RP scatter 3-4 times their errors, with isolated BP outliers above 2x (t=36.7, 237.8, 675.5, 833.5) not matched in G
Early pairs show FOV2 1-3% above FOV1 (t=76-141, 519-614) during the bright early part of the trend
BP depth 0.46 against G 0.048 and RP 0.036: an impossible combination, so the colour ratio is noise or BP systematics

explanation: Most likely a faint early-M dwarf (bp_rp 1.71, G-Ks 3.2, parallax SNR 3.3 implying M_G near 8) whose spot coverage changes. G drifts down about 5% over 2.7 yr (slope_z -4.9) but not smoothly (abbe 0.52, robust sigma 0.022, twice the errors). There are also short excursions, such as a drop of about 6% within hours near t=834.7 seen in both FOVs and partly recovered by t=898. This fits spot evolution or an activity cycle with rotational modulation on top. The colour test cannot help: BP and RP scatter 3-4 times their errors, and the BP depth of 46% is not physical next to a G depth of 4.8%. The WISE data are too noisy and show no IR excess. Instrumental drift or contamination of this faint source is the main alternative.

discriminating_test: Look for a rotation period of days to weeks in the dense ZTF plateau data or in TESS, and check for chromospheric or coronal activity (Ca II H&K or H-alpha emission, an eROSITA X-ray detection). A strong rotation signal plus activity confirms a spotted RS CVn-type star. A quiet, non-rotating photosphere points to a disk occultation.

evidence.feature: Gaia trend confirmed independently by ZTF g/r and NEOWISE W1 over a ~2200 d depression with flat levels before and after
ZTF-era depth ratios g/r ~1.29 and W1/r ~0.37, matching a single-temperature cooling prediction (~1.3, ~0.3)
W1 dims ~10% at the minimum, far more than interstellar-like dust predicts (~2-3%)
Gaia-era W1 slope (-0.049+/-0.0125/yr) matches the grey prediction and not the temperature prediction (-0.015); BP/RP ratio 1.34+/-0.45 is consistent with grey
Intrinsic short-term variability: sigma_visit 3.5%, coherent +11% brightening at t=180 in both FoVs and bluer in BP, ZTF bin minima 5-10% below medians
Photospheric IR colours (Ks-W1 0.1, W1-W2 0.0) and no W1/W2 brightening
Normal RUWE 0.95, ipd_frac_multi_peak 0, corrected BP/RP excess near zero
Duration of years is far too long for any stellar eclipse; no recurrence
Smooth fade of ~0.4 mag in g, not a deep, sudden multi-magnitude drop

explanation: Most likely an active, spotted (RS CVn-like) K subgiant or giant going through a long activity episode. The Gaia fade is the start of a ~2200-day, ~30%-deep depression that ZTF and NEOWISE W1 also show, and it returns to a flat level by about day 2600. In the ZTF era the depths go g:r:W1 ~ 1.29:1:0.37. Cooling a ~4500 K photosphere predicts ~1.3:1:0.3 with one parameter. Interstellar-like dust would leave W1 almost undimmed, and grey blocking would give g=r. Visit-to-visit scatter of 3.5%, including a +11% brightening at day 180 that is strongest in BP, shows the star varies on its own with temperature-like colours. The main alternative is a circumsecondary disk with grey plus small-grain dust.

discriminating_test: Pull the ZTF g/r (and ASAS-SN/Pan-STARRS) light curve for 2018-2024 and compare with field stars of similar magnitude: a continued fade with g-r reddening points to dust or stellar change, a recovery or flat level points to a Gaia-specific residual drift.

evidence.feature: Monotonic ~4.7% G decline from first to last epoch, both FOVs agree (no FOV offset)
Abbe 0.046, slope_z -21: smooth secular trend, not isolated low epochs
sigma_visit 0.26% ~ photometric noise: star otherwise quiet, no rotational scatter
BP depth 0.042+-0.014, RP 0.0165+-0.008, ratio 2.53+-1.48 (z_grey 1.0, z_dust 0.6): colour unconstraining, mildly reddening
M_G ~4-5.6 after plausible extinction (G 16.9, 1800 pc, bp_rp 1.42): dwarf/subgiant, not giant
ruwe 1.02, ipd_frac_multi_peak 0, BP/RP excess 1.25 normal: no resolved neighbour
Ingress-like fade over ~1000 d would need ~0.02 km/s for a sharp-edged occulter crossing a ~1 Rsun star; only a graded optical-depth structure works
Galactic latitude 0-5 deg, crowded field; BP/RP scatter 2-3x their errors
