ZTF flat after 2018 (changes < 0.1%), NEOWISE W1/W2 unchanged, no IR excess
Turnoff F star (bp_rp 0.81 reddened, M_G about 2.5-3) in or near the instability strip

explanation: The 'dip' is three sparse visits 0.3-0.8% low, no deeper than the star's own scatter (G robust sigma 0.0049, about 3x the quoted errors). Transits hours apart change by 1-2% (884.88 to 885.13: -2% in 6 h; 733.32 to 733.49: +1.5%), and the bright and faint excursions show up together in G, BP and RP (t=34.6, 884.88, 885.13). That points to real sub-day variability, most likely a delta Scuti or gamma Dor pulsator; this turnoff F star (M_G about 2.5-3) fits. A low-amplitude contact binary would also fit. Three faint visits in a row out of 17 is easy to get by chance, and the 44.5 d repeat is weak. BP/RP depths are pure noise, there is no fov offset, ZTF and NEOWISE stay flat, and there are no blend signs.

discriminating_test: Take an optical spectrum (or check archival spectra and the OGLE/ASAS-SN light curve). Halpha emission and an SMC radial velocity (~+150 km/s) would confirm a Magellanic Be star. A featureless or broad-line spectrum would instead point to an AGN.

evidence.feature: bp_rp -0.03 at G=15.4 with parallax_snr -1.1 and ruwe 1.03: a luminous, distant hot star
IR excess rising with wavelength (G-Ks 0.7, Ks-W1 0, W1-W2 0.3) but G-W1 only 0.7, star-like rather than quasar-like
NEOWISE W1/W2 vary together by about 40% peak-to-peak over years (robust sigma 0.12 vs err 0.03), high after the Gaia recovery
Dimming grey across G/BP/RP (ratio 0.93+-0.17, z_dust -4.6), and the two fields of view agree within each visit
Similar depths in G, BP and RP, with only isolated single-band outliers (RP at 452 d, BP at 593 d)
Irregular levels inside the episode (0.80-0.97 on ~30 d scales), further dips at 530-628 d, and 4-5% changes within 4 h in all bands
Long episode (378 d) with no flat bottom or symmetric shape and no repeat at fixed depth

explanation: A hot (bp_rp -0.03) source at G=15.4 whose parallax is consistent with zero must be very luminous (M_G near -3 at Magellanic-Cloud distance; the coarse latitudes fit the SMC). It has a modest IR excess that grows with wavelength (G-Ks 0.7, W1-W2 0.3), which looks like a free-free decretion disk, and is far too blue in G-W1 for an AGN. NEOWISE varies coherently by about 40% over years and brightens after Gaia recovers. Gaia shows irregular, grey dimming of 15-20% over about a year, extra dips at 530-628 d, and 4-5% changes within 4 h in all bands, then a quiet phase. This fits Be-star disk loss and rebuilding plus pulsation better than eclipses, dust or artefacts.

discriminating_test: Get a low-resolution spectrum to look for Ca II H&K or H-alpha chromospheric emission and measure v sin i, and run a period search on the dense ZTF g/r data for a rotation signal of a few days to weeks with g amplitude about 1.3 times r. Finding these would confirm a spotted active star; a grey multi-year fade with no rotation signal would raise disk occultation.

evidence.feature: sigma_visit 0.018 vs G errors ~0.004; few-day changes coherent within visits and across both FOVs, no FOV offset
ZTF g and r show multi-year ~5% swings (low t~2800-3300, recovery after ~3300); ztf_after change -1.7%/-2.2%
Independent W1 visits high (1.05-1.07) early in Gaia span then lower; W1 slope -0.025+/-0.016 per yr
Ks-W1 0.1, W1-W2 0.0: photospheric, no warm dust
ruwe 1.0, ipd_frac_multi_peak 0, bp_rp_excess 1.24 normal for colour
BP/RP depth ratio 0.91+/-0.46 (z_dust -1.74); no deep reddened fade
M_G ~3.7 from distance 3100 pc: subgiant, not a luminous giant
parallax_snr 6.7 and W1-W2 = 0
Detected signal is a slow trend with no recurring discrete dips

explanation: The star is a reddened G/K subgiant (M_G about 3.7 at 3.1 kpc) with no IR excess, and it varies on its own. Gaia visit-to-visit scatter is 1.8% against errors of 0.36%, the two fields of view agree, ZTF g and r change by a few per cent over days, and ZTF shows multi-year swings of about 5%: a low state around t=2800-3300, then a recovery. The Gaia trend (-3.1%/yr, about 8%) looks like one leg of that long-term variation. W1 being high early in the Gaia span backs this up. The likeliest cause is an active spotted star (RS CVn-like), with rotational modulation riding on an activity cycle. The colour ratio (0.91+/-0.46) and the W1 slope cannot tell grey dimming from a temperature change.

discriminating_test: Find an archival optical spectrum or H-alpha emission-line survey entry for the source. Balmer emission at zero (or SMC) velocity confirms a Be star. Broad redshifted lines would make it a QSO. A normal absorption-line B/A spectrum with no emission would shift weight toward instrumental causes or unexplained.

evidence.feature: parallax_snr 0.31 at G 15.9 with |b| 40-45 and |beta| 60-70 (SMC-like position): a luminous hot star, not a nearby dwarf
IR excess rising to longer wavelengths: G-Ks 0.1, Ks-W1 0.9, but W1-W2 only 0.1
NEOWISE W1 mean falls from ~1.06 (t<=615) to ~0.95 (t 786-2440), then returns to ~1.07; amplitude larger than the 4% G fade and lagging it
Fade present in G, BP and RP with similar depths (3.9%, 3.1%, 3.75%); ratio 0.82+/-0.30, z_dust -2.9
Slow trend with stochastic scatter (abbe 0.57, no repeating dips), not discrete eclipses
Some 2-3% G differences within 106.5-min FoV pairs are not mirrored in BP, so G errors are underestimated or crowding adds noise

explanation: Most likely a classical Be star, probably in the SMC. Coarse latitudes |b| 40-45 and |beta| 60-70, plus a parallax consistent with zero, put a G=15.9, BP-RP 0.05 source at M_G about -3, and its decretion disk is fading. The 4% fade is grey to slightly red (BP/RP 0.82+/-0.30, interstellar-type dust rejected at 2.9 sigma). NEOWISE W1 drops about 10% (about 5 sigma) soon after the Gaia fade and recovers after t~2600, more than G does, as expected when disk emission declines inside-out. The IR excess rises with wavelength (G-Ks 0.1, Ks-W1 0.9, W1-W2 0.1), as in Be disks. Stochastic percent-level scatter fits Be activity. A QSO is disfavoured by W1-W2 0.1 and G-Ks 0.1.

discriminating_test: Check the archival ZTF/ASAS-SN light curve for 2018-2023. An activity cycle predicts that the mean level recovers or keeps varying, with a colour ratio of about 1.4, while the ~1.5 d spot modulation continues and changes in amplitude. A dust occultation predicts a discrete event with a ratio of about 1.7 and no rotational link. Ca II H&K or Halpha emission in a spectrum would also confirm high activity.

evidence.feature: Smooth ~1.5 d, ~4% modulation at t=270-272.6 with BP/RP depth ratio ~1.4
Fade colour ratio 1.64+/-0.20 (z_grey 3.25, within ~1 sigma of 1.4-1.5 for a temperature change and of 1.7 for dust)
W1/W2 pre-fade visits (t<600) ~1.5-2.5% above in-fade visits (t=758, 952); W1 still low at t=1120
Pipeline NEOWISE test against all outside visits: W1 change -0.007+/-0.008, closer to the dust-in-front prediction
Gradual, irregular rise then decline over ~1000 d rather than a flat baseline with a discrete event
Both FOVs agree in pairs during the fade; calibration drift removed; ipd_frac_multi_peak 0 and normal BP/RP excess
No IR excess (W1-W3 ~0.1, W4 upper limit) and galactic latitude 35-40 deg
RUWE 3.15: probable companion that could host circumsecondary material
Single RP outlier at t=602.157 (1.037, while the other FOV gives 0.944)

explanation: This is most likely a magnetically active, fast-rotating G dwarf (M_G about 4.9, BP-RP 0.9) going through a slow change in spot coverage or an activity cycle. The dense run at t=270-272.6 shows a smooth ~1.5 d modulation of about 4% peak-to-peak. It is coloured (BP/RP about 1.4), so spots rather than ellipsoidal variation. The ~10% fade from t~226 to 978 has a similar colour (1.64+/-0.20, within about 1 sigma of a temperature change) and agrees between fields of view. Against the pre-fade NEOWISE visits, W1 and W2 dimmed by about 2-3%, which matches the temperature prediction better than dust in front. There is no IR excess, and the star sits at high galactic latitude.

discriminating_test: Use archival pre-2014 photometry (SDSS/Pan-STARRS epochs, plates, 2MASS vs AllWISE levels) to find when and how the fade began. A curved ingress from a flat baseline with some chromatic structure would favour disk occultation. A sharp onset into an exactly linear grey ramp would favour unexplained or injected. A current spectrum would confirm Teff is unchanged.

evidence.feature: Same fade rate (~2.5-2.8%/yr) in Gaia G, ZTF g/r/i, NEOWISE W1 and W2 over ~11 yr
Fade seen by four independent instruments with very different PSFs (Gaia, ZTF 2 arcsec, WISE 6 arcsec); ruwe 1.02, ipd_frac_multi_peak 0
BP/RP depth ratio 0.48+-0.3 (z_grey -1.7, z_dust -4.05); ZTF g, r, i fade alike
W1 fades by about as much as the optical (1.20 to 0.89), not the ~30% of G a cooling star predicts
Smooth monotonic trend (abbe 0.07, slope_z -15.1), quiet otherwise (sigma_visit 0.35%), no recurrence, still fading at the end of ZTF
Parallax SNR 17, M_G ~7.5 with bp_rp 1.48: a main-sequence K dwarf at high galactic latitude, normal BP/RP excess
Ks-W1 and W1-W2 ~0: no warm excess while ~26% of the light is lost, and W1/W2 do not brighten

explanation: A quiet main-sequence K dwarf (M_G about 7.5, parallax SNR 17, photospheric Ks/W1/W2) fades smoothly and linearly at about 2.5-2.8%/yr for more than 11 years. The rate is the same in Gaia G, ZTF g/r/i, NEOWISE W1 (about 26% over 10 yr) and W2, so it is grey from 0.48 to 4.6 micron. Independent instruments agree, which rules out instrumental causes. Grey dimming in W1 rules out a cooling star or spots (those predict about 30% of the G depth). ISM-like dust is excluded (z_dust -4). A slow ingress of large-grain or optically thick disk material is the only listed natural option. But a decade-long, curvature-free, perfectly grey ramp with no warm IR emission fits it poorly, so unexplained gets the most weight.

discriminating_test: Check independent 2014-2017 photometry (ATLAS, Pan-STARRS or CRTS) for the ~3% fade, and compare Gaia G of neighbouring stars of similar magnitude and colour in the same scans; a fade absent from other surveys means Gaia drift.

evidence.feature: Smooth monotonic G decline (abbe 0.13) present in both FoVs, no FoV offset
BP/RP depths 0.016+/-0.011 and 0.008+/-0.013 do not confirm the 2.6% G depth; RP early epochs near 1.0
Isolated epochs (t=171, 306, 831) with BP/RP ~+10-15% while G is normal
NEOWISE W1 -6+/-3% inside window (t=872 visit 8% low at 3% error), W2 rules out 1000 K shell
ZTF 2018-2025 flat to 0.2% with negligible slope; star otherwise quiet
Parallax SNR 5.5, W1-W2 ~ -0.3, bp_rp 0.78, G-Ks ~1.4: ordinary F/G dwarf at high latitude, no IR excess
Single long drop with plateau, no recurrence or eclipse-like shape

explanation: A smooth ~3% G fade over Gaia's first ~700 d (abbe 0.13, slope -1.7%/yr), then a plateau, on a quiet F/G dwarf (M_G ~4.5) with stellar colours and IR, ruwe 1.04, no multi-peak. Both fields of view share it, so no FoV offset. BP/RP are too noisy to set colour (ratio 2.0+/-3.8); excluding epochs where BP and RP jump ~11% with G unchanged (a neighbour in the larger windows), early RP shows little excess, so a residual Gaia G calibration/processing drift remains plausible. W1 is marginally low inside the window (-6+/-3%), hinting the dimming is real and temporary; ZTF 2018-2025 is flat. No single cause dominates: instrumental drift, a long shallow occultation, or a rare activity-scale change all remain open.

discriminating_test: Get an archival ground-based light curve (ASAS-SN or ATLAS) covering the episode dates. Check whether the ~50 d spot modulation continued through the depression with the same amplitude, and whether similar year-long low states recur irregularly (spot cycles of an active giant). The alternative is a single dusty occultation that dilutes the modulation. A spectrum showing Ca II H&K or H-alpha emission and fast rotation would confirm an active star.

evidence.feature: G agrees between fov 1 and 2 inside the episode (541.2: 0.891/0.896; 560.0: 0.943/0.939; 784.0: 0.942/0.946) and the dip spans 7 visits at different scan dates
sigma_visit 0.0266 against flux errors ~0.0023; 7.7% rise in 15 d (359 to 374.7) outside the episode; ZTF r shows quasi-periodic +/-4% swings (minimum ~2860-2868, maximum ~2889)
NEOWISE W1 change -0.0149 +/- 0.0112 against -0.080 predicted for grey blocking; W1 = 1.000 at t=578.6 while G was ~0.92
BP/RP depth ratio 1.31 +/- 0.32 (z_grey 0.97, z_dust -1.2), consistent with spot contrast on a ~4300 K star (~1.25)
Box-like ~8% depression with a fast ingress (1.03 at 374.7 to 0.917 at 408.5) and a return to normal by 915
No IR excess (Ks-W1 0.1, W1-W2 -0.1, W3/W4 upper limits); predicted 1000 K shell brightening of W1 (+0.65) not seen
Parallax SNR 2.8 at G 15.9 with normal RUWE implies a distant, luminous (evolved) star at |b| 20-25 deg
RUWE 0.996, ipd_frac_multi_peak 0, BP/RP excess factor normal for its colour
BP and RP jump 7-9% between fields of view at t=541 and 560 while G does not, so BP/RP are noisy or contaminated at some transits

explanation: Most likely the star's own variability: an active, spotted K star, probably a distant giant of the RS CVn type. It varies far more than its errors (sigma_visit 2.7%; 0.955 to 1.032 in 15 d before the episode; ZTF shows roughly 4% quasi-periodic swings on a ~50 d timescale). The 8% year-long depression looks like a change in its mean spot level. The G depths agree between fields of view, so an artefact is unlikely. NEOWISE W1 dimmed only 1.5 +/- 1.1%, where grey blocking predicts 8%. That rules out a grey occulter or eclipse but fits a cooling (spot) change, or small-grain dust in front. The BP/RP ratio of 1.31 +/- 0.32 cannot tell these two apart. The lack of an IR excess argues against a YSO or an RCB star.

discriminating_test: Check per-CCD AF G fluxes and window/IPD flags for the six in-dip transits, and the G light curves of nearby stars of similar magnitude and colour on the same transits. If the fade is missing from the raw CCD-level G (or shared with neighbours), it is an artefact or injection. If independent red-band photometry from days ~400-680 also shows a ~5% fade, the astrophysical classes come back.

evidence.feature: G depth 0.050+/-0.004 while RP depth -0.004+/-0.009 and BP -0.011+/-0.028; at the deepest transit G -8.5% while RP +2.4% and BP +2.2%
Dip coherent in both fov 1 and fov 2 and smooth across several visibility periods (abbe 0.19), not a single-epoch or scan-angle pattern
phot_bp_rp_excess_factor 1.3 matches expectation for bp_rp 1.74, ipd_frac_multi_peak 0, ruwe 1.0: no neighbour in the BP/RP windows to dilute a real change
A band-inconsistent G-only change is the kind of signature a G flux processing problem could leave
No IR excess (Ks 14.3, W1 14.1, W2 14.3, W3/W4 upper limits); colours fit a reddened late-K/early-M dwarf at 980 pc
Single asymmetric episode (ingress ~50 d, slower egress ~100-200 d), no repeat in 996 d
NEOWISE W1/W2 change has only one in-episode visit and errors larger than any prediction

explanation: The dip is a smooth fade in G alone, about 5% deep (8.5% at t=455), lasting roughly 150-280 d, and both fields of view agree. In the same transits BP and RP do not dim: RP depth is -0.004 +/- 0.009 and at t=455 RP=1.024, BP=1.022. G covers the same wavelengths as BP plus RP, so any real change on the star (occultation, dust, cooling, spots) has to show in RP. Here a 5% fade is ruled out at about 5 sigma. Nothing points to a blend: excess factor normal for this colour, ipd_frac_multi_peak 0, ruwe 1.0. Most likely this is a G-only signal that no listed process produces (likely injected). Second most likely is a G-only processing artefact.

discriminating_test: Take one spectrum to measure Ca II H&K emission (S-index) and lithium. Alternatively, run a period search on the dense ZTF seasons for a days-to-weeks rotation period whose amplitude and mean level follow the multi-year swings. Strong chromospheric activity would confirm a spot or activity cycle.

evidence.feature: W1 slope -0.0017+-0.0019/yr vs grey prediction -0.0105 and temperature prediction -0.0033
BP/RP depth ratio 1.26+-0.30 (between grey and dust; matches a cooling/spotted photosphere)
ZTF multi-year quasi-cyclic variation, g amplitude about twice r, recovering by t~3800
Large intrinsic short-term scatter (robust_sigma 1.3% vs 0.16% errors; 1.7% change in 6 d; s_rep period 24 d)
Trend present in both fov 1 and fov 2; calibration drift removed; ruwe 1.04, ipd_frac_multi_peak 0
No IR excess (W1-W2 = 0, W3/W4 upper limits), high galactic latitude, main-sequence luminosity
Only 20 Gaia visits; ZTF per-field normalisation can create offsets between seasons

explanation: A quiet-astrometry K dwarf (M_G about 5.4, bp_rp 1.14, no IR excess) fading about 2.8% over 986 d. The most likely cause is a magnetic activity cycle, with spot coverage changing over years, on top of rotational modulation. G scatter is 1.3% against 0.16% errors, with 1.7% changes within 6 days. BP/RP = 1.26+-0.30 fits a temperature or spot change. Flat NEOWISE W1 (-0.0017+-0.0019/yr) rules out grey blocking at about 4.6 sigma and matches the temperature prediction. The fade appears in both fields of view. ZTF later shows quasi-cyclic, multi-year swings of 3-4% in g and about 2% in r (bluer is larger), with a recovery by t~3800. That is what a cycle predicts, not a one-off occulter.

discriminating_test: Check Gaia epoch photometry of nearby stars of similar magnitude and colour on the same scans for steps near t~170, 520 and 760 d (shared steps mean calibration). Then check whether ZTF g/r from 2018 on shows the star still faint and redder, which would favour dust occultation.

evidence.feature: BP/RP depth ratio 2.47+/-0.43 (z_grey 3.46, z_dust 1.81), with BP falling about 8% and RP about 3.5% over the span
G depth (0.0316) falls between the BP and RP depths, consistent with a real colour change of the source's light
Fields of view 1 and 2 agree within each visit group in G; ipd_frac_multi_peak 0, ruwe 1.02, BP/RP excess normal for the colour
Three sharp steps, each inside a gap of 26-42 d, separating plateaus flat to about 0.3%
Fade is monotonic and does not recur (s_rep weak at 551 d)
Distance 1.1 kpc and G 15.6 imply a dwarf or subgiant, not an evolved giant; depth only about 5%
No WISE photometry, no NEOWISE visits during the fade, no ZTF coverage: IR re-emission and continuation cannot be checked

explanation: A reddened, probably F/G dwarf or subgiant (M_G about 4) with clean astrometry and a normal BP/RP excess fades in three abrupt steps (about -1.5%, -1.0%, -2.2%) between flat plateaus over 992 d, about 5% in G in total. The two fields of view agree, so a blend that depends on scan angle is unlikely. The fade is chromatic: BP/RP = 2.47+/-0.43 rules out grey blocking (3.5 sigma) and spots (about 1.2), sits in mild tension with stellar cooling (about 1.5), and fits small-grain dust (1.8 sigma from ISM-like). G lies between BP and RP as expected. The leading explanation is progressive occultation by structured dust. The flat plateaus with sharp steps also look like calibration offsets, and there are no IR, NEOWISE or ZTF data to test, so a large share of the probability stays elsewhere.

discriminating_test: Compare each G transit's flux with its scan angle, and list Gaia sources within about 4 arcsec. If the bright epochs share a scan-angle range that puts a neighbour along the scan, it is a blend. If they do not, check the ZTF r PSF light curve for ongoing irregular variability of 5-10%, which would point to an intrinsic giant.

evidence.feature: phot_bp_rp_excess_factor 1.53 for bp_rp 2.51, |b| 0-5 deg, G=17.6
BP fov1 vs fov2 within one scan: 3.08 vs 1.28 at t=0, 1.66 vs 0.82 at t=733; BP robust sigma 0.21 vs error 0.053
RP robust sigma 0.052 is 4x its error and 4x the G scatter, the reverse of what intrinsic variability of a red star gives
G differs between fields of view in the same scan by about 3% at t=567 (1.039 vs 1.007) and t=965 (0.986 vs 1.017)
Bright state at t=0 and 164-215 interrupted by a normal visit at t=34; later flat near 1.0; abbe 0.62
Parallax SNR 0.63 with red colour and G-Ks about 4.5 rules out a nearby M dwarf and suggests a distant reddened giant
Single 607-day low state with no repeats; 26.2 d rep period from only 15 visits
BP/RP depth ratio -1.12 +/- 6.79, so the colour is unconstrained; no WISE or NEOWISE data

explanation: The 'drop' is really a few early bright G visits (t=0 and 164-215, about 7-13% above a flat later level), with a normal visit at t=34 between them, so it is not a clean fade. The source is faint, red and distant (parallax SNR 0.63) at Galactic latitude 0-5, with an elevated BP/RP excess (1.53). Its BP and RP scatter is 4-16 times their errors, and BP changes by a factor of about 2 between the two fields of view within 106 min (t=0, t=733), which marks a contaminated window. The likeliest cause is flux from a neighbour that enters the window at some transits. The main alternative is irregular variability of a reddened giant. The colour is unconstrained and there is no infrared or recurrence data.

discriminating_test: Get the per-transit scan angles and the Gaia DR3 sources within ~4 arcsec. If the faint-G, bright-BP transits (145, 394, 878, 903) share scan angles that point at a neighbour, it is a blend. Also check that ZTF r/i PSF photometry shows no 3-9% dips.

evidence.feature: BP flux 18.6x and 16.1x median at 878.8 and 902.9, and 3.5x and 2.6x at 394.6 and 145.2, while G dims at 145, 394 and 878
colour_of_change: depth_bp -0.71 (brightening), depth_rp 0.005+-0.012, depth_g 0.032+-0.006; RP normal or high at the 394.6 and 676.7 G dips
fov 1 fainter than fov 2 in 8 of 10 same-day pairs (e.g. 676.68 0.932 vs 676.76 0.979; 300.14 0.981 vs 300.21 1.008); deep lows mostly single fov-1 transits
n_below_3sigma 5, n_above_3sigma 0: one-sided faint outliers, typical of window-edge or truncated-window flux loss
Dip window 394-878 holds many normal visits; abbe 1.13, slope_z -0.6: no smooth dimming episode
rep_period 30.4 d, close to half the 63 d precession period, from only 22 visits
W1-W2 = -0.2, W3/W4 only upper limits: no warm dust or disk excess; G-Ks ~7 at |b|<5 means a heavily reddened cool star
G = 18.8, BP noise-dominated (err ~0.5), galactic plane: crowded field where neighbours enter the BP/RP windows

explanation: The 484-day 'episode' is not a coherent fade. It is a handful of isolated single-transit G lows (394.6, 676.7, 701.9, 878.8, plus 0, 145) with normal visits in between (409, 524, 556, 733, 773, 783), and abbe is 1.13. The lows sit mostly in fov 1, and fov 1 is fainter than fov 2 in 8 of 10 pairs. All G outliers are faint (5 below, 0 above), which looks like flux loss. RP barely dims (0.005+-0.012 vs G 0.032). BP jumps 2.6x, 3.5x and 18x at the G-dip transits 145, 394 and 878. No occulter or star does that. This is a faint, very red, reddened plane star with no IR excess, and the likeliest cause is crowding or window flux loss at certain scan angles. The 30.4 d repeat is near the 63 d scanning-law alias.

discriminating_test: Check whether the bright first-year Gaia G epochs (88-357 d) share a scan-angle range or a calibration interval that later epochs lack, and compare with neighbouring stars of similar magnitude and colour. A scan-angle or neighbour-shared step would move the weight to blend or calibration. If neither shows, a measured rotation period and chromospheric activity (Ca II H&K or X-ray) would confirm spot or activity variability.

evidence.feature: Smooth multi-year level change of about 1.5% (abbe 0.30, slope_z -6) that returns to the median at the last epochs; no sharp ingress or egress
Star is intrinsically variable: G robust sigma 0.0083 against errors of 0.0017, sigma_visit 0.0045, s_rep period 22 d
BP/RP depth ratio 1.92 +/- 0.83, consistent with both cooling (about 1.5) and dust (1.7); grey is only 1.1 sigma away
NEOWISE W1 change +0.004 +/- 0.006 against a grey prediction of -0.017 and a 1000 K shell prediction of +0.127; W2 is too noisy to decide
fov1 and fov2 G pairs agree within a few mmag throughout, so there is no field-of-view offset
Galactic latitude 0-5 deg; BP has several single-transit excursions of +4 to +9% (for example 937.455 fov2) while G stays steady, suggesting a neighbour in the BP/RP window at some scan angles
ruwe 1.01, ipd_frac_multi_peak 0 and a normal BP/RP excess factor, so no close resolved companion is evident
In ZTF, g dims more than r in the first season (about 3-5% in g), with no level change after 2020
W1-W3 = 0.8 is a weak possible excess, but W3 is near its limit in the Galactic plane, there is no ir_excess_sigma and the IR SED is otherwise photospheric

explanation: A reddened K-type dwarf (M_G about 6.4 before extinction at 600 pc) that is variable on its own: G scatter about 5 times its errors, visit noise 0.45%, a 22 d repeat signal consistent with rotation. The 'drop' is a shift of about 1.5% in mean level between the first year (88-357 d) and later, which is smooth, slow and returns to the median by 988 d. Both fields of view agree and BP and RP both follow it. The colour ratio of 1.9 +/- 0.8 is consistent with the star cooling. NEOWISE shows no W1 drop (disfavours grey blocking) and no warm-shell brightening. ZTF shows chromatic few-percent wander (g deeper than r) and no lasting fade. The likeliest cause is spot or activity-cycle evolution, with a residual Gaia calibration or crowding systematic second.

discriminating_test: Pull the archival ZTF g/r light curve (2018 on). A return to the pre-fade level through a smooth grey egress would point to a disk occultation. Continued stochastic wandering of tens of per cent would point to a quasar or intrinsic variability. A flat light curve at the old level would point to a residual Gaia artefact. An archival spectrum would also settle hot star versus quasar.

evidence.feature: ratio_bp_over_rp 0.858+/-0.265 (z_grey -0.5, z_dust -3.2): grey fade
Fade seen in G, BP and RP with similar depth (0.038/0.033/0.038) and in both fields of view
ruwe 1.0, ipd_frac_multi_peak 0, bp_rp_excess 1.15 normal: no sign of a neighbour
Ks 16.8 so G-Ks ~ -0.5; no AllWISE match and no NEOWISE detections: hot-star SED, no IR excess
parallax_snr -1.1, bp_rp ~0 at |b| 40-45: distant blue source (halo BHB or quasar)
Earlier ~1% hump (days 150-460) and smooth wandering, abbe 0.107: red-noise-like variability before the fade
Fade still under way at the last visit, no egress, s_rep weak (4.89 at 639 d)
Pairs 106.5 min apart differ by ~1% against 0.3% errors: errors underestimated, so some wiggles are noise

explanation: The source looks like a distant hot star: BP-RP is about 0, the parallax is consistent with zero, Ks=16.8 gives G-Ks of about -0.5, and WISE and NEOWISE detect nothing. It fades smoothly by about 4% from day ~640 to the end, in both fields of view and in G, BP and RP alike. The BP/RP depth ratio of 0.86+/-0.27 is grey, which rules out interstellar-like dust (z_dust=-3.2) and cooling. With ruwe 1.0 and no multi-peak, a blend is unlikely. My best guess is a long grey occultation by a large-grain disk around a companion, with no egress yet. A quasar would match the red-noise shape and the earlier ~1% hump, but its infrared SED would be far redder. A residual Gaia trend remains possible.

discriminating_test: Phase-fold all Gaia and ZTF epochs at P = 2.4197 d and at 2P = 4.839 d. Check that a single coherent flat-bottomed primary eclipse appears. Compare odd and even minima, and look for a secondary eclipse near phase 0.5 (or check a periodic-variable catalogue for an EA at this period).

evidence.feature: Gaia and ZTF dip times are integer multiples of ~2.4197 d apart over ~4000 d (e.g. 1754.60->3939.60 = 903 P, 1442.47->3327.41 = 779 P, Gaia 5.15/302.79/694.78 on the same ephemeris)
Repeated minimum depth ~0.72-0.76 in G, BP, RP, ztf_g, ztf_r; BP/RP depth ratio 1.05 +/- 0.89 (grey)

Dip duration ~4-5 h: both FoV transits at 302.74/302.81 in eclipse, 145.43/145.60 at 5%/3% at ingress/egress edges, adjacent nights normal; consistent with t ~ 2R/v for a ~2.4 d orbit (a ~ 9-10 Rsun, (R1+R2)/a ~ 0.24)
Ks, W1, W2 photospheric for bp_rp 0.92; W3/W4 only upper limits; star ~1 kpc above the plane
ipd_frac_multi_peak 0, ruwe 0.97, normal BP/RP excess; same ~27% depth in the small Gaia G window and in the ~2 arcsec ZTF PSF
Detected episode's 3.2% depth comes only from the two endpoint eclipse epochs; the 12 interior visits average ~1.00 (abbe 1.08, slope_z ~0)
ZTF median level after 2020 vs 2018-2019 is unchanged (+0.8% g, +0.5% r)

explanation: Detached eclipsing binary. The 392-d 'episode' is not a sustained fade: its 3.2% mean deficit comes entirely from two short eclipse epochs at its ends (302.8, 694.8). The 12 visits between them average about 1.00. All the deep dips (Gaia 5.15, 145.5 edges, 302.8, 694.8, and about 40 ZTF g/r events from 1362 to 3973) fall on one strict period, P ~ 2.4197 d (e.g. 1442.47->3973.48 = 1046 P; 694.78 = 1442.47 - 309 P), or 4.84 d if the two eclipses are twins. The eclipses are about 4.5 h long with a flat floor near 0.72-0.76 in G, BP, RP, ztf_g and ztf_r (grey). The photosphere is normal in the IR, and the astrometry shows no blend.

discriminating_test: Phase-fold all Gaia and ZTF epochs on P = 3.2489 d (or check VSX and the Gaia DR3 eclipsing-binary table at this position) to confirm a primary at phase 0 and a red secondary at phase 0.5.

evidence.feature: Deep (~0.28-0.35 G) short (<0.4 d) dips at t=96.4, 476.6, 694.3 and ZTF 1733.9, 1759.8, 2123.8, 2529.8 all fit a single period of ~3.2489 d
Shallow ~0.87-0.89 dips at phase 0.50 (t=146.9, 384.0, 679.6; ZTF 2219.6, 2170.8, 3265.7, 3502.9) with RP deeper than BP: secondary eclipses of a cooler companion
Primary minima slightly deeper in BP than RP (e.g. 0.244/0.365 at t=96.44; 0.300/0.404 at t=694.28); colour ratio 0.79+/-0.40 is near grey, not dust
Out-of-eclipse epochs inside 384-694 d sit near 1.0; the 8% visit-mean deficit comes only from eclipse epochs, and the 197-d rep_period is a sampling alias
Same ~72% maximum depth in Gaia G and ZTF r PSF photometry; ruwe 1.06, ipd_frac_multi_peak 0, normal BP/RP excess
Brightest epochs (t=0, 79.4, 357.2) fall near phases 0.25/0.75
No IR excess (W1-W2 ~ -0.2, W3/W4 upper limits); NEOWISE change consistent with zero

explanation: Algol-type eclipsing binary. The 310-d 'dimming episode' is an artefact of averaging eclipse epochs into visit means: the out-of-eclipse baseline inside the window stays near 1.0. Every deep epoch in Gaia and ZTF (t=96.4, 476.6, 694.3, 1733.9, 1759.8, 2123.8, 2529.8) folds on P ~ 3.2489 d. The primary eclipse is ~72% deep, lasts ~0.35 d, and is slightly deeper in BP (hot star eclipsed). Shallow ~12% dips (t=146.9, 384.0, 679.6, ZTF 2219.6, 3265.7, 3502.9) fall at phase 0.50 and are deeper in RP: the cool secondary is occulted. Brightest epochs sit near quadrature (ellipsoidal or reflection effect). ZTF's 2-arcsec PSF photometry shows the same depths, and ruwe and ipd_frac_multi_peak are clean, so this is not a blend.

discriminating_test: Find out whether and when the star recovered and whether the fade repeats. Check Gaia DR4 epoch photometry (which extends past t=994) and absolute, unnormalised 2018 photometry (Pan-STARRS or ZTF zero-pointed magnitudes) against the pre-fade Gaia level. Also take one spectrum to look for youth or disk signatures (H-alpha, Li) and test whether the W3 excess is real.

evidence.feature: Fade coherent in time and seen in both fov 1 and fov 2 transits at the same depth
Dense transit groups at t=233-243 and 615-626 at normal flux, but the comparable group at t=993 is about 7% faint
Depth consistent in G (0.086), RP (0.070) and BP (0.16+/-0.07); ratio 2.32+/-1.17 (z_grey 1.13, z_dust 0.53)
Gradual ingress of about 150 d and duration over 164 d; t ~ 2R/v would need about 0.03 km/s for a stellar-size occulter
Otherwise quiet: Gaia pre-fade scatter about 1%, ZTF r robust sigma equal to its errors, ztf_after changes under 1.5%
Chromatic fade (BP deeper) on a cool M dwarf is also what a spot or temperature change predicts; NEOWISE W1 -0.031+/-0.041 is consistent with that
W1-W3 = 1.7 mag but W1-W2 = 0.0 and W3 near detection limit at low galactic latitude
Parallax SNR 28, M_G about 10.4 places it on the M-dwarf main sequence
Parallax well measured, point source

explanation: A mid-M dwarf (M_G about 10.4, BP-RP 2.49, RUWE 0.94) fades by about 8.6% in G over roughly 150 days from t of about 700. It stays faint (0.91-0.93) through Gaia's last visit at t=994. The fade shows in both fields of view, in RP (7%) and in BP (16+/-7%). Earlier dense scan groups (t=233-243 and 615-626) were at normal flux while the t=993 group is faint, which argues against a scan-angle blend or an offset between fields of view. The BP/RP ratio of 2.3+/-1.2 fits either dust or cooling, and NEOWISE is too noisy to choose. Outside the fade the star is quiet, and ZTF is flat from 2018 to 2025. The most likely cause is one long occultation by circumstellar dust (weak W3 hint). A spot or activity change, or a Gaia calibration artefact, is close behind.

discriminating_test: Get the per-transit scan angles and the Gaia sources within about 4 arcsec. If the early bright and faint G/BP outliers sit at scan angles that put a neighbour into the window, the drop is a blend artefact. A flat ZTF r light curve across the same span would also rule out a real fade.

evidence.feature: FoV pair at t=195.6/195.7 differs by 31% in G and by 9x in BP within 106.5 min
Band depths inconsistent: BP 0.86+-0.19, RP -0.002+-0.05, G 0.087+-0.011; G should track RP for BP-RP 3.67
G, BP and RP outliers anticorrelated at the same transit (t=34: G 0.94, RP 1.28, BP 3.19; t=0: G 1.39, RP 1.03)
phot_bp_rp_excess_factor 2.1 (well above normal for this colour), ipd_frac_multi_peak 4%, |b| < 5 deg, no WISE match
RP robust scatter (4.8%) larger than G (2%) in a very red star
Drop defined by early outliers; later 30+ epochs flat at about 2%; detection is a 162 d 'repeat' from only 18 visits
Very red G-Ks = 6.1 with Ks 11.3 suggests a reddened giant, which could add slow low-level variability (slope -4.5%/yr, z=-1.8)

explanation: The 'drop' is really a handful of wildly scattered early G epochs (1.39, 0.94, 1.07, 0.93/1.25, 0.96) followed by quiet data at about 2%. One FoV pair 106.5 min apart differs by 31% in G and ninefold in BP (0.69 vs 6.35). No star does that. The bands disagree: BP 'depth' 0.86, RP about 0, G 0.087. For a star this red (BP-RP 3.67), G should follow RP. At t=34, G is faint while RP and BP are bright. This is a faint, reddened source in the Galactic plane with a BP/RP excess factor of 2.1, multi-peak windows and no WISE match: a crowded field. The likeliest cause is a neighbour's flux entering the windows at some scan angles, or transits mis-assigned to this source.

discriminating_test: Compare the Gaia scan angles of the low transits (t=33, 80, 89) with the normal ones, and inspect why G was rejected at t=33. If the deficits track one scan angle, it is a neighbour or window artefact. If not, check Pan-STARRS or other photometry from the same period for an 8% dimming lasting months, and later ZTF or Gaia DR4 for a recurrence.

evidence.feature: Depth 7% held on fov 1 and fov 2 transits at t=79.86-80.11, then a monotonic recovery at t=89 and t=129
Episode lasts at least 50 and probably about 130 days (t=0 low, t=33 BP/RP low): duration needs an occulter much larger than the star
Dense t=239-245 sampling flat to about 0.5%, robust sigma 0.005: the star is otherwise quiet
Parallax SNR 6 at 2.5 kpc gives M_G about 4: not a giant
Ks-W1 about 0.1, no near/mid-IR excess, b 5-10 deg at z about 300 pc
BP/RP depths 0.061+-0.023 / 0.011+-0.017; ratio 5.3+-8.3 is uninformative (z_grey 0.52, z_dust 0.44)
At t=80 and t=89, G is slightly deeper than BP and RP, a weak hint of a G-window-only effect
RUWE 1.03, ipd_frac_multi_peak 0, BP/RP excess factor 1.21 is normal for bp_rp 0.98
305 d repeat score rests on only one strong event; no second episode in the 995 d

explanation: The star is a quiet F/G turnoff star (M_G about 4, RUWE 1.03, no multi-peak, normal BP/RP excess, no W1/W2 excess). It shows one smooth, months-long, shallow fade: G 0.988 at t=0, BP/RP about 6-12% low at t=33 (G rejected), G 0.93 on both fields of view at t=80, 0.954 at t=89 and 0.994 at t=129, with a flat baseline afterwards. A dimming that lasts 100 days or more is far too slow for a stellar or planetary eclipse (a star-sized body would need v of about 0.15 km/s). The occulter must therefore be extended, about an AU across: most likely a circumsecondary disk or a dust structure crossing in a long-period orbit. The colour is consistent with grey or dust (z of about 0.5 each). Some scan-angle blend artefact is possible but less likely.

discriminating_test: Extract ZTF g and r light curves of nearby stars of similar magnitude and colour on the same fields and CCDs to see whether the 2021-2024 fade is shared. If it is not, look in TESS for rotational spot modulation or flares that would confirm an active star.

evidence.feature: Smooth monotonic Gaia trend (slope_z -9.4, abbe 0.22) continuing as a multi-year quasi-cyclic variation in ZTF g and r
Fade deeper in BP than RP (ratio 6.8+-4, z_grey 1.44) and deeper in ZTF g than r
Colour ratio also consistent with interstellar-like dust (z_dust 1.26)
W1-W2 = 0.0, Ks-W1 = 0.1: no warm inner-disk excess (W3 mild excess likely plane contamination)
Same sense of slow variation in Gaia and ZTF PSF photometry; ruwe 0.95, ipd_frac_multi_peak 0
RP depth (0.23%) small relative to G depth (1.06%) for a red star; modest BP/RP excess factor in the Galactic plane
No dip epochs inside the Gaia fade; no recurrence of a fixed-depth eclipse; amplitude only a few per cent over years
M_G about 5.5 before extinction at 840 pc in the plane: reddened dwarf/subgiant or PMS star, not a giant

explanation: The 'dip' is one segment of a slow, smooth (Abbe 0.22), multi-year variation: Gaia G declines about 1.5% over 2.7 yr, then ZTF shows a high state around 2019-2020, a fade to about 5% in g and 3% in r peaking near t~3340, and partial recovery, which looks quasi-cyclic on roughly 6 yr. The fade is deeper in blue (BP/RP 6.8+-4, consistent with dust or cooling at about 1.3 sigma; ZTF g deeper than r). It appears in two independent instruments, so a single-survey artefact is unlikely. The most likely cause is a spot/activity cycle on a reddened, somewhat overluminous G/K star; slowly varying dust extinction comes second. There is no W1-W2 excess, so a dusty inner disk is unlikely. The mildly small RP depth relative to G is the only oddity.

discriminating_test: Pull the 2018-2024 ZTF g and r light curves (and a TESS sector for a rotation period). If the slow 1-3% wander continues, with g amplitude about 1.3-1.5x r and a short spot-rotation period, it is activity on the star. If ZTF is flat, a Gaia-only systematic is indicated; then check whether the G residuals correlate with scan angle.

evidence.feature: G light curve rises and falls (about 1.015 at days 256 and 638, about 0.99 at days 401-454 and 778-940): quasi-cyclic, not a linear fade
M_G about 6 minus extinction with bp_rp 1.46 at b 5-10 deg: reddened G/K main-sequence dwarf, not a giant
Ks, W1, W2 flat (Ks-W1 0.1, W1-W2 -0.1): no warm dust or disk
Colour ratio 2.85 +- 3.66 and NEOWISE slopes with large errors: cannot separate grey, dust and temperature
ipd_frac_multi_peak 0, ruwe 1.09, BP/RP excess 1.27 (normal for colour): no sign of a resolved neighbour
Weak repeat at 64.8 d (s_rep 3.1), close to the 63 d scanning-law precession; single-transit BP excursions of 7-9% between paired FoVs
slope_z only -4 with red noise present (abbe 0.40); modest significance for a large search
No detected discrete dips; depth 2% over 995 d with no eclipse shape

explanation: A reddened K dwarf: parallax SNR 22 at 1.1 kpc gives M_G about 6 before extinction, and there is no IR excess (Ks-W1 0.1, W1-W2 -0.1). The 'trend' is not a monotonic fade. G wanders by 2-3% peak to peak, quasi-cyclically: high near days 0-260 and 616-638, low near 400-450 and 778-940, recovering by day 994, a timescale of about 400 d. The fit is modest (slope_z -4 against white noise, abbe 0.40). The most likely cause is spot or activity-region evolution on an active dwarf. Colour (BP/RP ratio 2.85+-3.66) and NEOWISE slopes are uninformative. No eclipse-like structure. A residual source-level systematic (scan-angle contamination at low latitude, calibration) remains possible but is not indicated: ipd_frac_multi_peak 0, normal BP/RP excess, ruwe 1.09.

discriminating_test: Get a dense near-IR or I-band light curve of the star from a Galactic-plane survey (e.g. VVV Ks or OGLE I) to confirm ongoing semi-regular red-giant variability of a few per cent, and plot the Gaia G epochs against scan angle to rule out neighbour contamination of the trend.

evidence.feature: parallax_snr 1.3 with G=17.3, BP-RP 2.79, G-Ks 4.7 at |b|<5: a distant reddened giant, not a dwarf
G scatter of a few per cent between visits weeks apart (1.065 at t=0, 0.99 at t=34, 1.04 at t=164 and t=568) as well as the slow decline: the star varies all the time, the drop is not a one-off
Detected change is a gradual 'bright first, fainter later' trend of 2.3% (slope -1.74%/yr, slope_z -3.15, abbe 0.80), not a dip shape that returns to baseline
The two fields of view agree within each transit pair (e.g. 1.029/1.029 at t=188, 0.991/0.999 at t=915)
phot_bp_rp_excess_factor 1.52 is well above the expected ~1.32 for this colour, and BP/RP outliers occur where G is normal (BP 1.24 at t=591, RP 1.16 at t=784)
Negative BP and RP depths driven by those blend outliers; with them removed, RP falls with G, so the colour test does not show a real colour reversal
ruwe 0.935 and ipd_frac_multi_peak 0 show no resolved neighbour in the G window, so contamination is likelier in BP/RP than in G
ZTF r after Gaia is flat within its ~3% noise (change -0.04%), and ZTF g is too noisy for a very red faint star; no deep or recurring dips appear later
No WISE match and no IR excess information, so dust-shell scenarios cannot be tested directly

explanation: This is a distant (parallax SNR 1.3), reddened red giant in the Galactic plane (BP-RP 2.79, G-Ks 4.7). Its G light curve varies by about 3% from visit to visit on 30-200 d timescales and also declines slowly by about 4% over 965 d. The 'drop' is the end of that decline, not a separate event, and this is ordinary semi-regular or irregular giant variability. The two fields of view agree within each pair. BP and RP seem to brighten only because of single blend outliers (BP 1.24 at t=591, RP 1.16 at t=784, both while G was normal). That fits the significant BP/RP excess in a crowded field. Without those outliers, RP follows G. Remaining risk: neighbour flux that depends on scan angle, or residual calibration drift.

discriminating_test: Run a periodogram on the TESS or ZTF photometry for a coherent rotation period of a few days whose amplitude changes from season to season. A clear spot-modulation period, or Ca II H&K emission in one spectrum, would confirm an active spotted star.

evidence.feature: G light curve shows irregular +/-1-2% excursions with recoveries (e.g. 0.982 at 485 d back to 1.009 at 556 d), not a steady decline; abbe 0.34
ZTF g and r season medians vary by a few per cent in step with each other; ztf_after shows no continued fade (+0.4%, +0.6%)
BP/RP depth ratio 1.34 +/- 0.51, and ZTF g amplitude larger than ztf_r
NEOWISE W2 slope +0.013 +/- 0.004 per yr against a grey prediction of -0.0105; W1 matches the temperature prediction
No IR excess (Ks-W1 = 0, W1-W2 = -0.1, W3/W4 upper limits)
Distance 880 pc and G = 15.1 give M_G about 5, so a dwarf, not an evolved giant
fov 1 and fov 2 agree at each faint visit (e.g. 840 d: 0.968/0.972; 688 d: 0.979/0.978); ipd_frac_multi_peak 0, ruwe 1.05, normal BP/RP excess
Low galactic latitude (5-10 deg) leaves room for a neighbour; scan angles are not given
Excess scatter of about 0.5% within single days (t = 0-1.2, 556, 577 d) beyond the quoted errors
Lone BP outlier at 864 d (0.939) not matched in G or RP

explanation: The detected 'trend' is not a monotonic fade: G wanders irregularly by +/-1-2% on ~100-300 d timescales (faint near 420-485, 655-690, 790-865 d, recovering in between), and ZTF g/r show season-to-season changes of similar size later, with no continued fade after 2020. The star is a near-main-sequence G/K dwarf (M_G about 5, ruwe 1.05, no IR excess). Both fields of view and all three Gaia bands agree. The dips are mildly chromatic (BP/RP 1.34, ZTF g amplitude larger than r), which fits cool-spot or activity modulation. NEOWISE W1 matches a temperature-like change, not grey blocking. The most likely cause is spot evolution or an activity cycle on an active star, with crowding or residual calibration as the main instrumental alternatives.

discriminating_test: Take one low-resolution optical spectrum now and JHKs photometry to compare with 2MASS (1998-2001). Unchanged photospheric lines with dust-like reddening (A_K/A_g ~0.1) and circumstellar Na D / K I absorption would mean an occulting dusty structure. A lower Teff in the photospheric lines would mean an intrinsic change. Near-grey dimming out to K would mean large grains or an opaque partial cover.

evidence.feature: Monotonic fade with abbe 0.023 and slope_z -39.4 in Gaia G, continuing in ZTF g (about 1.18 to 0.69) and r (about 1.12 to 0.79) through t~4030, in hundreds of epochs across several fields
The same fade in Gaia G, BP and RP, ZTF g and r, and NEOWISE W1: several independent instruments
BP/RP depth ratio 1.45 +/- 0.39, with ZTF g fading faster than r (mag ratio ~1.5): the dimming reddens the star
ruwe 1.02, ipd_frac_multi_peak 1%, BP/RP excess 1.24 as expected for a single star of bp_rp 1.25
No near- or mid-IR excess (Ks-W1 ~0.1, W1-W2 ~0.0) and |b| 15-20 deg at 1400 pc
M_G ~5.4-5.7 with bp_rp 1.25: a K dwarf or subgiant, not a luminous giant or supergiant
W1 fell ~13% over the decade (mostly before t~1100), much more than small-grain dust in front predicts (a few % of the optical depth); the total is closer to what stellar cooling predicts
Very quiet from visit to visit (sigma_visit 0.3%; groups within a day agree to ~1%) despite a 0.5 mag fade
A smooth fade lasting at least 11 yr cannot come from a sharp edge crossing the star; it needs an optical-depth gradient spanning AU scales

explanation: This is a real, smooth fade lasting about ten years. Gaia G drops 9% over 2.5 yr (abbe 0.02, slope_z -39). ZTF continues it to about -0.58 mag in g and -0.38 mag in r by t~4030. The BP/RP and g/r depth ratios (~1.45-1.5) mean the light gets redder. Independent instruments rule out calibration, and clean astrometry and a normal BP/RP excess argue against a blend. The star looks like a quiet K dwarf or subgiant (M_G~5.5) with no IR excess, which disfavours YSO, R CrB and giant variability. The leading explanation is a large dusty structure (circumstellar or circumsecondary disk) slowly moving across the star, getting thicker as it goes. But W1 also faded ~13%, more than small-grain dust predicts, so intrinsic cooling or something not listed remains possible.

discriminating_test: Get the per-transit scan angles and the Gaia sources within about 5 arcsec. If the deviant fov-1 transits (33.88, 168, 196, 219, 388.7) share scan angles that put a neighbour in the window or at its edge, the cause is crowding. If not, a ZTF r/i light curve showing slow 5-10% semi-regular variation would favour a pulsating giant.

evidence.feature: All five extreme G epochs (33.88, 168, 196, 219, 388.7) are fov 1; the fov 2 points stay within 0.974-1.019
At t=33.9 fov1 G=0.949 and fov2 G=0.991, 106 min apart (about 4.6 sigma)
RP depth -0.039+/-0.018 (it brightens) while G dims by 0.077; RP is not bright at 168-196
RP robust sigma 0.038 against 0.011 errors; BP/RP excess factor 1.71 (about 3-4 sigma above the expectation for this colour); |b| < 5 deg
The deviations are epoch-specific: later fov1 points agree with fov2, so there is no constant FoV offset
BP-RP 3.79, G-Ks 5.9, parallax SNR -0.25: a distant reddened giant, not a nearby M dwarf
Slow structure (abbe 0.60) and a repeat near 314 d, a timescale typical of semi-regular giants and long secondary periods
The change is a 600-day low plateau after a bright run, not a dip with a U or V shape

explanation: The 'drop' is really three bright single-transit G points (t=168-219, about 1.075) set against a flat later baseline near 1.0. All five strongly deviant G epochs (0.949, 1.072, 1.075, 1.079, 0.945) are field-of-view-1 transits. In the one pair that tests this, fov1 sits 4% below fov2 within 106 min, which no giant star does. RP does not follow G: its depth is -0.039+/-0.018, so it brightens rather than dims. RP also scatters at 3.5 times its errors. Add the galactic-plane field and the raised BP/RP excess, and the likeliest cause is crowding that depends on the transit, a neighbour in or at the edge of the window. The star, a distant reddened giant (parallax consistent with zero), may still vary slowly in a semi-regular way.

discriminating_test: Check Legacy Survey or Pan-STARRS images for a neighbour within about 2 arcsec, and plot Gaia G/BP/RP flux against scan angle. Also check asteroid ephemerides (SkyBoT) at the 88x-flux transit time to confirm it was a solar-system body.

evidence.feature: depth_g 0.0306 +/- 0.0269, slope_z -0.87: drop consistent with noise
single G epoch at 88.4x flux (fov 2), RP 2.9x, near the ecliptic
ipd_frac_multi_peak = 1.0 (double image in all transits)
BP brightens (-0.55 +/- 0.18) while RP and G barely change: opposite-sign colour change
RP at t=561: fov1 0.60 vs fov2 1.68 within 106 min; G at t=155: 1.07 vs 0.97
ZTF r flat within noise over 2680 d, +8.6% after 2020 (insignificant)
no 2MASS/WISE counterpart, so no IR excess test possible

explanation: The detected 3% drop is not significant: depth_g 0.031 +/- 0.027 (about 1 sigma) at G=20.6 with only 8 visits. The 'bright at first' baseline is set by one transit at 88x flux (t=134.9, fov 2 only, RP 2.9x), most likely an asteroid (ecliptic latitude 0-10 deg) or a mis-matched transit, plus a 1.07 fov-1 point. That outlier also drives the repeat score. ipd_frac_multi_peak = 1.0 says every transit sees a double image, and the anticorrelated BP (-0.55) and RP (+0.12) changes, together with large fov-to-fov jumps in RP, point to neighbour contamination that depends on scan angle. ZTF r (255 epochs) shows nothing beyond noise. So the most likely cause is a blend plus a spurious pipeline detection, not a dip on the star.

discriminating_test: Lomb-Scargle the ~1200 ZTF r epochs (and any TESS sectors) by season to look for a stable 2-5 d rotation period whose amplitude and mean level follow the multi-year brightness changes. Chromospheric emission (H-alpha, Ca II) would also confirm the spotted-star reading.

evidence.feature: Smooth ~3.5% fall and recovery over ~2 days at t=252-254, tracked by both FoVs and RP
sigma_visit 0.0155 vs G errors ~0.003; ZTF robust_sigma 0.031-0.034 vs errors 0.011-0.015
ZTF g and r faint (0.92-0.97) in 2019 recovering gradually to ~1.0-1.04 after 2020, continuing the Gaia decline
BP/RP depth ratio 1.44 +/- 0.85, consistent with cool spots (also with dust)
Ks-W1 0.2, W1-W2 -0.1, W3/W4 upper limits: bare photosphere
Distance 1100 pc and G=16 give M_G ~5.3-5.8: a dwarf, not an evolved star
NEOWISE W1 slope +0.0125/yr vs predicted -0.018 (grey) and -0.006 (temperature), from 5 sparse visits
ruwe 1.71 with ipd_frac_multi_peak 0 and mildly high BP/RP excess
